Alternatively, you can add the report to the Vault in RightCapital which the client can then access through the RightCapital client portal.

Email Option: Dear [Prospect], Thank you for signing up for a 30-minute introductory meeting with me on [date and time] via [a Zoom invitation]. The intent of our meeting will be for me to learn how I might be able to assist you through my guidance and a comprehensive financial plan and for you to learn about my firm and the various engagement choices I offer. Our goal at the end of this complimentary meeting will be to determine if we want to schedule a deeper dive discovery meeting, in which I can learn about the nuances of your current situation and goals. I’ll also have time to reflect on our first discussions to share some possible high-level recommendations. At the end of the meeting, we should know enough to decide whether working together makes sense. Find attached a proposed agenda for our 30-minute meeting and a [brief questionnaire](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/420) to help me know you a bit better before we meet! I look forward to meeting with you on the [Date and Time] via [Zoom]. Warm regards, [Your Name]

Connect with your prospect in person, by phone, or through video. Use this opportunity to identify their needs and goals. Hold Discovery Meeting
steps.description: Identify your prospects' needs during this meeting. Brainstorm solutions for their main challenges and to address both short- and long-term goals. Apply the 80/20 Rule: spend 80% of the time listening and 20% talking during client conversations. Focus on understanding their needs, concerns, and goals. Use open-ended questions to encourage them to share more. This builds rapport and helps you tailor your solutions. Share relevant success stories to highlight your value. Use this agenda for [talking points](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/371) . Recap what you’ve discussed and show how you’ve supported others in similar situations. Ask if they need anything else to move forward. Aim for a verbal agreement and discuss the next steps before sending an electronic agreement for signing.

steps.name: January
steps.description: This month, the focus is on cash flow and budgeting, including reviewing credit reports. Email Option: Subject: Important Topics to Start the Year! Dear [Client Name], I hope you’re having a great week! As we move into the year, we’re eager to share some intriguing topics and insights that will be the focus of our upcoming communications and activities. The first is understanding your cash flow and keeping a consistent budget. This is key towards reaching your financial goals. Regularly reviewing your income, expenses, and credit report can help you spot trends, catch potential issues early, and make confident decisions about saving and spending. If you would like assistance, wish to discuss any updates, or need some accountability to help you stay on track, please let us know. Thank you for your continued trust in us. Best regards, [email signature]

This month, the focus is on tax prep and tax return review. Email Option: Subject: Tax Preparation & Return Review Hi [Client Name], As tax season is here, I want to ensure your tax preparation goes smoothly and that we review your final return to optimize any potential tax savings. While I don't prepare taxes directly, I can coordinate with your tax preparer or assist you if you file yourself, ensuring they have all the necessary information regarding your investments and other relevant details. After your return is complete, we will review it together to identify planning opportunities, reduce future tax liability, and align your tax strategy with your long-term financial goals. Let me know if you need help gathering documents or if you’d like me to coordinate with your tax professional. Best, [Your Name]
steps.name: February

steps.description: This month, the focus is on debt management, with a review of net worth and the balance sheet. Regularly reviewing your balance sheet and net worth help to ensure that your decisions align with your long-term goals. By examining your assets and liabilities, we can see if debt is helping you or if it is holding you back. This helps us find ways to lower interest costs, improve flexibility, and increase your net worth over time. If you have any questions or want to discuss this in detail, I’m happy to schedule some time. My goal is to make sure every part of your financial plan is aligned and moving you forward with confidence. Best regards, [Your Name]

steps.name: June
steps.description: This month, the focus is on reviewing the estate plan, including document review (wills, trusts, POAs, advance directives), beneficiaries, and gifting strategies. Email Option: Subject: Important Touchpoint for Your Estate Planning Dear [Client Name], As we continue our planning journey together, I wanted to reconnect about your estate plan and beneficiary designations. My goal is to ensure that your documents and strategies genuinely reflect your wishes and seamlessly integrate with your overall financial plan. Let’s confirm that your beneficiary designations are up-to-date, evaluate essential documents like wills, trusts, powers of attorney, and advance healthcare directives, and explore gifting strategies that align with your aspirations and offer potential tax advantages. Whether you’ve experienced a recent life change or it has simply been a while since we last reviewed these items, now is an ideal time to ensure your coverage still aligns with your goals. Thoughtful planning in this area fosters clarity, continuity, and peace of mind for you and your loved ones. Please let us know if you’d like to have a conversation about any of these topics. Best regards, [Your Name]

It’s a great time to make sure your donations are working effectively for both your legacy and your tax return. [I invite you to set up a 30-minute virtual meeting with me. Email Option: Dear [Prospect], Thank you for signing up for a 30-minute introductory meeting with me on [date and time] via [a Zoom invitation]. The intent of our meeting will be for me to learn how I might be able to assist you through my guidance and a comprehensive financial plan and for you to learn about my firm and the various engagement choices I offer. Our goal at the end of this complimentary meeting will be to determine if we want to schedule a deeper dive discovery meeting, in which I can learn about the nuances of your current situation and goals. I’ll also have time to reflect on our first discussions to share some possible high-level recommendations. At the end of the meeting, we should know enough to decide whether working together makes sense. Find attached a proposed agenda for our 30-minute meeting and a [brief questionnaire](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/420) to help me know you a bit better before we meet! steps.name: Send Reminder Email

steps.description: Connect with your prospect in person, by phone, or through video. Use this opportunity to identify their needs and goals. The insights you gather will let you customize your services and offerings to align with their objectives. Present your firm's key attributes and pricing, then propose a 'deeper dive' Discovery meeting to explore further. Use this [meeting guide](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/372) to outline the agenda and key topics. Provide a [service calendar](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/1151) to show clients your dedication to their success and that support is provided in a timely manner throughout the year. Keep the meeting to about 30 minutes, using the 80/20 Rule: spend 80% of the time listening and 20% talking. If your prospect shows interest and values your offerings, you can extend the conversation as needed. Offer to schedule a time for their Discovery meeting if they are a good fit.

steps.description: Send an [email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/423) to thank your prospect for their time, recap the main topics discussed, and share a relevant piece of content. Confirm the date and agenda for the upcoming Discovery meeting, and include some thoughtful questions for them to consider beforehand. If the prospect was a referral, send a thank-you note to your source. Email Option: Subject: Excited for Our Next Steps Together! Hi [Client's Name], I wanted to take a moment to express my heartfelt thanks for the wonderful meeting we had recently. It was great to explore our common ground and share ideas together. As we look ahead to our next meeting, I’m really looking forward to diving deeper into your financial goals and working together to create a personalized strategy just for you. It’s going to be an exciting journey! I’ve included an [ [agenda](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/371) ] for our meeting to provide clarity on the flow of our discussion and enhance our time together. Also, take a look at this [blog I wrote on a topic they expressed interest in.] Please feel free to reach out if you have any questions or need assistance with anything. I can’t wait to continue our conversation! Warm regards, [Your Name]

Identify your prospects' needs during this meeting. Brainstorm solutions for their main challenges and to address both short- and long-term goals. Apply the 80/20 Rule: spend 80% of the time listening and 20% talking during client conversations. Focus on understanding their needs, concerns, and goals. Use open-ended questions to encourage them to share more. This builds rapport and helps you tailor your solutions. Share relevant success stories to highlight your value. Use this agenda for [talking points](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/371) . Recap what you’ve discussed and show how you’ve supported others in similar situations. Ask if they need anything else to move forward. Aim for a verbal agreement and discuss the next steps before sending an electronic agreement for signing.

Level Up Your Relationship
localResources.emailBody:
Hello!

This is exciting. You want to get on the same page with your partner and start doing finances like you mean it. That tells me that you are ready to level up your relationship. Congratulations!

Also, thank you so much for becoming a subscriber, I am so happy to have you here.

To get started, download the guide to Marrying Your Finances👇

DOWNLOAD YOUR GUIDE HERE

By downloading this guide and answering the questions you will be on the right track to setting a great foundation for your partnership. Don’t hesitate to reach out to me if you run into any questions along the way.

Talking about money isn’t sexy but that feeling when you’re on the same page is! 👌

I just want to say one more time, thank you so much for subscribing. I am honored to have you here and can't wait to be a part of your journey.

Talk soon!

Hi there!

Being able to talk about money and work through uncomfortable conversations is the mark of a strong partnership. Whether you're dating, planning your wedding, or have been married for years, it's never a bad time to learn more about your partner.

Learning about each of your relationships to money tells you more about what you each fear and value in life. This will help you more easily discuss future plans and form shared goals as a couple.

Before we dive in, consider these tips:
Set aside time to talk in advance.
Make sure you’re both comfortable and at ease. (No hangry money talks!)
Keep it short enough that you’ll want to do this again.
Make it your goal to be purely curious about your partner’s responses and feelings.
Take decision-making off the table. Deep dive discussions are best treated as exploratory missions, not business meetings.
If it gets too tense, call it off and circle back again with refreshed gentleness and curiosity when it feels like a better time.
Now you’re ready to try some of these discussion prompts and dive deeper learning about each other. 

10 Deep Dive Discussion Prompts
What’s your earliest money memory?
How was money saved, managed and allocated in your family growing up?
What’s important about money to you?
Have you ever felt like you didn’t have enough money? When and why?
Have you ever felt like you had enough money? When and why?
Are there financial topics or expenses you consider private? Why?
What scares you about combining finances?
What excites you about combining finances?
What is the biggest financial decision you’ve made? How did you make that decision? Who did you turn to for advice?
What does financial success look like to you? How will you know that you’ve arrived at it?
If you really dove in, you might have only made it through one question on this list. That’s great! If your first go at a deep dive money conversation didn’t feel like a great success, that’s OK too. Go easy on yourselves - this is new territory and you have a lifetime ahead to keep trying.

No matter the outcome, the fact that you’re here means you care deeply about your relationship and that is something to celebrate!

Until next time,

This Work Matters to Me
localResources.emailBody:
Hello,

I’d like to back up a bit and introduce myself. My name is Kaylin. 🙋🏻‍♀️ I started my financial planning firm to help couples with prenuptial agreements and blended families because I believe being willing to talk about having separate financial interests is something to celebrate. ♥️

Let me tell you more about why this work is so important to me…

 When my dad died his life insurance policy was supposed to name my sister and me as the beneficiaries according to his divorce agreement with my mom. It turned out he had changed the beneficiary to his new wife. I was a teenager, and this was my first time learning that there’s no one out there making sure people stick to their legal agreements. It seemed bizarre to me that the only mechanism to enforce an agreement is to pursue someone legally after they’ve broken it. Surely lots of people don’t even mean to break their agreements, right? 🤷🏻‍♀️

When my husband and I got married we first signed a prenuptial agreement. By that point I’d already learned that it was up to us to make sure we upheld the terms of our own agreement. We didn’t have an authority figure reminding us how to title our accounts and property, paying attention to which accounts should receive what type of income deposits, or making sure we maintain life insurance, as we’d agreed to do. But I started thinking: wouldn’t it be nice if we did?

Financial advisors are in a unique position to help families proactively keep family law out of their family’s choices.

Whether it’s for a divorce or a marriage, couples don’t enter into marital agreements lightly. This is why I care about helping couples uphold the agreements they’ve made all the while helping them plan confidently for their future together.

Best,

localResources.emailSubject: Do I need a prenup? 👉 Your free guide is inside
localResources.emailBody:
Hello Couples,

You’re planning your future together. Congratulations! Hopefully, you’re also having the oh-so-fun conversations about how you’ll manage your finances during marriage. You may now be wondering, how do I know if I need a prenup? Or if you weren’t wondering that, you may now be wondering, aren’t prenups only for celebrities?

Prenups are not just for the ultrawealthy - and they aren’t just for divorce! Prenuptial agreements are great ways to be completely transparent about finances before marriage. They can also be used to plan for how you’ll manage finances during marriage and what will happen to your assets when a spouse dies.

Still not sure if a prenup is right for you? I’ve created a guide for you.

Download the guide here. 👇

Do I need a Prenup?

For better or for worse, your marriage is a financial partnership. If you and your partner don’t create a custom prenuptial agreement, you automatically get a default “prenuptial agreement” in the form of your state’s laws. That’s not necessarily a bad thing, but it’s best to opt in to your state’s treatment of your marital and separate property intentionally.

Don’t hesitate to reach out to me with any questions you have during this process.
localResources.name: Do I Need a Prenup?
5 Myths About Prenuptial Agreements
localResources.emailBody:
Hi There!

Prenups are not exactly a common dinner topic. For that reason, myths and misconceptions about prenuptial agreements have been able to persist for a long time. But I’m here to help dispel some of those myths.

Did you hold any of these misconceptions?

Myth #1: Prenups are only for divorce.
Prenups are not only created to protect assets in the event of a divorce. You can include terms in your prenup to:
Determine how you’ll share or divide income during marriage.
Set a formula to compensate a spouse if they become a stay-at-home parent.
Direct where your assets will go when you die.
Require your partner to maintain a life insurance policy (and name you as the beneficiary).
Myth #2: Prenups only benefit the wealthier spouse.
Prenups do not only protect the assets of the wealthier spouse. Prenuptial agreements are actually a great way for the spouse with fewer assets to make sure they have protections set up for the future, including spousal support in the event of a divorce.

Myth #3: If you really love each other you won’t ask for a prenup.
Prenuptial agreements are a great way to be transparent and realistic about your future marriage. Divorce rates are as high as ever and what could be more loving than saying you want to make sure your partner is treated fairly no matter what the future holds. Marriage is full of uncomfortable conversations and less-than-sexy realities. Talking about money and how to treat it is just one of them. Why not decide what’s fair now while you love and respect each other?

Myth #4: Prenups aren’t necessary if you don’t have money.
Prenuptial agreements can protect money and property you bring to the marriage but they can also protect:
Future inheritance
Shares in a family business
Your rights to your pet
Your credit report
If one spouse is coming to the marriage with debt or you’re worried about one spouse accumulating debt, you can set rules for whether or not you’ll take on that debt with them. For example, you can stipulate that any debt accumulated without your signed consent belongs solely to the spouse who took out the loan or credit card.

Myth #5: You can accomplish the same goals by keeping your money separate.
Keeping your money in separate accounts does not necessarily make that money separate property in the eyes of the state. Every state law is different so it’s a good idea to consult an attorney if your plan was to go the separate account route. In many cases, separate accounts are considered marital property even if it was only in one spouse’s name.

Thanks for tuning in. Let me know if you have any questions or want help creating a financial summary before marriage.

If being realistic and committed is the highest form of love, you’re on the right track!

Until next time,

Subject: Your First Meeting Coming Up Body:

Hi {{216899441__invitee_first}},

I enjoyed chatting with you to learn more about your situation and needs, along with what’s most important to you. During our conversation, these were the most pressing issues that you shared you would like to address:

{{216899853__formFields__Brief_summary_of_pressing_issues_or_goals_shared_by_prospect:}}

If there is anything you would like to change or add, simply let me know.

Our process is designed to help create a simple, easy-to-understand plan that will address these and any other items that we may uncover. This meeting, typically 60–75 minutes, is a chance for us to dive deeper into your specific financial situation and goals.

To ensure our time together is well spent, we need access to several specific financial documents and basic financial information. Click here to securely upload the following documents at least 6 days prior to the meeting:

  • Retirement plan statements (e.g., IRA, 401(k), 403(b), 457, etc.)
  • All other investment account statements
  • Last two years’ tax returns (personal and business if applicable)
  • Social security statements (If needed, go here to locate and download: social security site)
  • Pension Benefit Statements
  • Any Other Financial Documentation You Feel Is Helpful

As always, if you have any questions in the interim, we would welcome a call from you anytime. Look forward to seeing you soon.

In your service,

Danny Michael

Personal Video Introduction
steps.description: Introducing yourself and showing your commitment to their financial success builds trust and engagement. This enhances your credibility and creates a positive environment for discussing goals, which is crucial for converting leads into valued clients. Email Option: Subject: A warm message from [Your Name]. Hi [First Name], I wanted to share a quick video [insert link to website] to let you know why I’m so passionate about helping people reach their financial goals. Take a moment to watch, and I’d love to hear your thoughts. I look forward to supporting you on YOUR journey! Ready to go? [insert scheduling link] Warm regards, [Your Name]

steps.name: Provide a Resource (Lead Magnet)
steps.description: Lead prospects to your website whenever possible. Provide a resource or use a lead magnet (example below) to capture a prospect's email address. A lead magnet helps firms gain visibility, foster relationships, and increase sales. Email Option: Subject: More Value! Hi [Client Name], I'm excited to keep our connection going! We know that financial planning can feel overwhelming, but we're here to help you navigate it with confidence. To get started on the right foot, we invite you to explore this free resource on our website [insert link - example lead magnet below]. It’s a great way to learn more about our approach and some key considerations as you begin your financial journey. Ready to begin? [insert scheduling link] Warm regards, [Your Name] Lead Magnet Example: Get the Clarity You Need to Make Smarter Financial Decisions Feeling unsure about whether you're on track with your money? You’re not alone. That’s why I created this free resource — a simple, actionable guide that helps you get organized, understand your next steps, and feel more confident about your financial future. Inside, you’ll learn: What to focus on right now How to avoid common financial mistakes Easy steps you can take to improve your financial life When it makes sense to get professional support It’s completely free — no jargon, no overwhelm. Just practical guidance you can use today. 👉 Enter your email to get instant access.

steps.name: Addressing Common Concerns
steps.description: Addressing frequently asked questions and common concerns shows your commitment to clients' needs. This makes you a reliable resource and boosts engagement from potential clients. Email Option: Subject: Is Your Money Putting in the Same Effort You Do? Let's tackle a prevalent misconception that often hinders individuals! Many believe, “I don’t have enough to invest,” or “investing carries too much risk.” The reality is that there are customized solutions for every financial circumstance! Here’s a [blog/article] I wrote on this topic. I am here to assist you every step of the way! Here’s my link for when you’re ready to chat! [insert scheduling link] Warm regards, [Your Name]

Knowing and communicating your services helps clients understand them better and positions your offerings effectively, encouraging action when they are ready. We are excited to present our personalized financial planning services tailored just for you! Our expert [investment, tax planning strategies] are thoughtfully crafted to align with your unique challenges and aspirations. You can view all our services here: [insert link to website]. localResources.name: 🕸️ WB: XYPN 2: Prospect to Client - NEW DUPE

steps.description: Send an email to express appreciation for their outreach. In this [email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/411) , provide a link to your calendar to schedule a 30-minute introductory meeting (if not already scheduled), outline its purpose, and include a relevant piece of valuable 'fee-only' content. Email Option: Dear [Prospect], Thank you for reaching out to [Firm Name]. We help individuals in [niche] manage their finances and reach their goals while overcoming challenges. [I invite you to set up a 30-minute virtual meeting with me. This will give me the chance to learn more about what you want from a financial advisor.] During our meeting, I will explain the services we offer at [Firm Name]. If you think my services might be a good fit for you, we can schedule a complimentary, in-depth discovery meeting to discuss your primary life goals. I will then suggest solutions to help you achieve those goals. [If this sounds good, please pick a time on my calendar [insert link].] In the meantime, I recommend reading [this article] about how fee-only services are different from traditional brokerage firms. My priority is to put your interests first and help you live your best life. I look forward to hearing from you. Warmly, [Your Name]
steps.name: Lead Follow-Up
Send Reminder Email
steps.description: Send a [reminder email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/422) , including an agenda for the introductory meeting and a [brief questionnaire](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/420) . Remind your prospect that the meeting's purpose is to learn about each other and determine a mutual fit for working towards their goals. Email Option: Dear [Prospect], Thank you for signing up for a 30-minute introductory meeting with me on [date and time] via [a Zoom invitation]. The intent of our meeting will be for me to learn how I might be able to assist you through my guidance and a comprehensive financial plan and for you to learn about my firm and the various engagement choices I offer. Our goal at the end of this complimentary meeting will be to determine if we want to schedule a deeper dive discovery meeting, in which I can learn about the nuances of your current situation and goals. I’ll also have time to reflect on our first discussions to share some possible high-level recommendations. At the end of the meeting, we should know enough to decide whether working together makes sense. Find attached a proposed agenda for our 30-minute meeting and a [brief questionnaire](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/420) to help me know you a bit better before we meet! I look forward to meeting with you on the [Date and Time] via [Zoom]. Warm regards, [Your Name]

steps.name: Hold Prospect Meeting
steps.description: Connect with your prospect in person, by phone, or through video. Use this opportunity to identify their needs and goals. The insights you gather will let you customize your services and offerings to align with their objectives. Present your firm's key attributes and pricing, then propose a 'deeper dive' Discovery meeting to explore further. Use this [meeting guide](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/372) to outline the agenda and key topics. Provide a [service calendar](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/1151) to show clients your dedication to their success and that support is provided in a timely manner throughout the year. Keep the meeting to about 30 minutes, using the 80/20 Rule: spend 80% of the time listening and 20% talking. If your prospect shows interest and values your offerings, you can extend the conversation as needed. Offer to schedule a time for their Discovery meeting if they are a good fit.

steps.name: Prospect Meeting Follow-Up
steps.description: Send an [email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/423) to thank your prospect for their time, recap the main topics discussed, and share a relevant piece of content. Confirm the date and agenda for the upcoming Discovery meeting, and include some thoughtful questions for them to consider beforehand. If the prospect was a referral, send a thank-you note to your source. Email Option: Subject: Excited for Our Next Steps Together! Hi [Client's Name], I wanted to take a moment to express my heartfelt thanks for the wonderful meeting we had recently. It was great to explore our common ground and share ideas together. As we look ahead to our next meeting, I’m really looking forward to diving deeper into your financial goals and working together to create a personalized strategy just for you. It’s going to be an exciting journey! I’ve included an [ [agenda](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/371) ] for our meeting to provide clarity on the flow of our discussion and enhance our time together. Also, take a look at this [blog I wrote on a topic they expressed interest in.] Please feel free to reach out if you have any questions or need assistance with anything. I can’t wait to continue our conversation! Warm regards, [Your Name]

steps.name: Hold Discovery Meeting
steps.description: Identify your prospects' needs during this meeting. Brainstorm solutions for their main challenges and to address both short- and long-term goals. Apply the 80/20 Rule: spend 80% of the time listening and 20% talking during client conversations. Focus on understanding their needs, concerns, and goals. Use open-ended questions to encourage them to share more. This builds rapport and helps you tailor your solutions. Share relevant success stories to highlight your value. Use this agenda for [talking points](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/371) . Recap what you’ve discussed and show how you’ve supported others in similar situations. Ask if they need anything else to move forward. Aim for a verbal agreement and discuss the next steps before sending an electronic agreement for signing.

steps.name: Discovery Meeting Follow-Up
steps.description: Send the follow-up information to convert your prospect into a client. Include your proposal from the meeting. Thank them for their trust and express your excitement about collaborating to achieve their goals! Encourage them to sign the agreement by a specific date so you can schedule a "Get Organized" meeting. Email Option: Dear [Client], I truly appreciate the opportunity to meet with you today! Your openness about your life goals was inspiring, and I am genuinely excited about the prospect of collaborating. I will be sending over the formal agreement for your electronic signature shortly. Once signed, we can arrange our first "Get Organized" meeting, during which I will guide you on the necessary documents to prepare. Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any questions before our meeting. Thank you for allowing me to be part of your journey toward achieving your goals! Best regards, [Your Name]

steps.name: January
steps.description: This month, the focus is on cash flow and budgeting, including reviewing credit reports. Email Option: Subject: Important Topics to Start the Year! Dear [Client Name], I hope you’re having a great week! As we move into the year, we’re eager to share some intriguing topics and insights that will be the focus of our upcoming communications and activities. The first is understanding your cash flow and keeping a consistent budget. This is key towards reaching your financial goals. Regularly reviewing your income, expenses, and credit report can help you spot trends, catch potential issues early, and make confident decisions about saving and spending. If you would like assistance, wish to discuss any updates, or need some accountability to help you stay on track, please let us know. Thank you for your continued trust in us. Best regards, [email signature]

steps.name: February
steps.description: This month, the focus is on tax prep and tax return review. Email Option: Subject: Tax Preparation & Return Review Hi [Client Name], As tax season is here, I want to ensure your tax preparation goes smoothly and that we review your final return to optimize any potential tax savings. While I don't prepare taxes directly, I can coordinate with your tax preparer or assist you if you file yourself, ensuring they have all the necessary information regarding your investments and other relevant details. After your return is complete, we will review it together to identify planning opportunities, reduce future tax liability, and align your tax strategy with your long-term financial goals. Let me know if you need help gathering documents or if you’d like me to coordinate with your tax professional. Best, [Your Name]

This month, the focus is on debt management, with a review of net worth and the balance sheet. Email Option: Subject: A Quick Check-In on Your Debt & Overall Financial Picture Hi [Client Name], I'd like to check in on your debt and how it impacts your overall finances. Regularly reviewing your balance sheet and net worth help to ensure that your decisions align with your long-term goals. By examining your assets and liabilities, we can see if debt is helping you or if it is holding you back. This helps us find ways to lower interest costs, improve flexibility, and increase your net worth over time. If you have any questions or want to discuss this in detail, I’m happy to schedule some time. My goal is to make sure every part of your financial plan is aligned and moving you forward with confidence. Best regards, [Your Name]
steps.name: March
April
steps.description: This month, the focus is on preparing for the Spring Review meeting and reviewing goals. Email Option: Subject: Financial Planning Meeting Dear [Client Name], I hope you are having a wonderful week. It’s time to schedule your Spring Review meeting. During this meeting, we'll [brief description of meeting purpose or agenda]. Please upload the following items to your client portal: [portal link] [enter items needed for this meeting] Once you've uploaded those items, please complete our meeting prep form [insert link to pre-meeting prep form]. Be sure to add any additional items you wish to discuss and I will make sure we have those on the agenda. [After completing the form, you'll find a link to schedule a meeting on the confirmation page. ] Have a great week, and I look forward to seeing you. Best regards, [email signature]

steps.name: May
steps.description: This month, the focus is on insurance coverage and analysis (life, disability, home, auto, umbrella) . Email Option: Subje ct: In surance Review Hi [Client Name], I wanted to connect regarding your overall plan, focusing on your insurance coverage. My goal is to ensure these components align with your long-term aspirations. Major life milestones, such as a career change, a new addition to the family, or a move to a new home, often impact your insurance needs. These shifts are a critical time to reassess your disability, life, home, auto, and umbrella coverage to ensure your protection still aligns. If you’d like to discuss these topics or if there have been recent changes in your circumstances, I’d be happy to schedule some time with you. Thoughtful coordination can reduce risk and enhance your financial clarity! Best regards, [Your Name]

steps.name: June
steps.description: This month, the focus is on reviewing the estate plan, including document review (wills, trusts, POAs, advance directives), beneficiaries, and gifting strategies. This is one of my favorite times of the year, as it gives us the opportunity to thank you for the trust you place in us and to spend time together outside of our regular meetings. Event Details: 📅 Date: [Event Date] ⏰ Time: [Event Time] 📍 Location: [Event Location or Virtual Link] We’re planning an enjoyable [brief description] with great conversation, light refreshments, and a chance to connect with other clients and our team. Feel free to bring a guest; we’d love to meet the people who matter most to you. Please let us know if you’re able to attend by [RSVP Date]. You can RSVP here: [RSVP or Registration Link]. I hope you can join us, and I look forward to seeing you there. Warm regards, [Your Name]

This month, the focus is on tax planning, including charitable contributions, Roth conversions, capital gain and loss harvesting, and tax projections for the upcoming year. Email Option: Subject: Year-End Tax Planning Check-In Dear [Client Name], With year-end approaching, I’d like to check in on your tax planning and charitable giving goals. It’s a great time to make sure your donations are working effectively for both your legacy and your tax return. [For those 70½ and older, we can look into Qualified Charitable Distributions as a tax-savvy giving tool.] We can also review your portfolio for capital gains or losses and discuss whether a Roth conversion or rollover makes sense for your long-term plan. To help us get a head start, please share any updates regarding your income or retirement accounts. It’s also helpful to know about any large investment sales or estimated tax payments you’ve made recently. If a Roth conversion is on your radar, let’s chat about your current tax bracket and cash flow for any potential tax hits. We are here to help. Contact us with any questions you may have. Best, [Your Name]

steps.description:
Subject: Your First Meeting Coming Up Body:

Hi {{216899441__invitee_first}},

I enjoyed chatting with you to learn more about your situation and needs, along with what’s most important to you. During our conversation, these were the most pressing issues that you shared you would like to address:

{{216899853__formFields__Brief_summary_of_pressing_issues_or_goals_shared_by_prospect:}}

If there is anything you would like to change or add, simply let me know.

Our process is designed to help create a simple, easy-to-understand plan that will address these and any other items that we may uncover. This meeting, typically 60–75 minutes, is a chance for us to dive deeper into your specific financial situation and goals.

To ensure our time together is well spent, we need access to several specific financial documents and basic financial information. Click here to securely upload the following documents at least 6 days prior to the meeting:

  • Retirement plan statements (e.g., IRA, 401(k), 403(b), 457, etc.)
  • All other investment account statements
  • Last two years’ tax returns (personal and business if applicable)
  • Social security statements (If needed, go here to locate and download: social security site)
  • Pension Benefit Statements
  • Any Other Financial Documentation You Feel Is Helpful

As always, if you have any questions in the interim, we would welcome a call from you anytime. Look forward to seeing you soon.

In your service,

Danny Michael

Welcome & Introduction
steps.description: This outreach piques your audience's interest and sets the stage for deeper engagement throughout the campaign. It enhances the overall experience and establishes a strong foundation for a successful journey together. In addition, including a newsletter or blog in your drip campaign is crucial for audience engagement. It allows prospects to receive regular updates, valuable resources, and exclusive content, improving their overall experience. Email Option: Your Path to Financial Confidence Starts Here! Hello, and welcome! It’s great to connect with you! I want to introduce myself and my team at [Firm Name]. We are excited to have you in our community. We are committed to empowering individuals like you through our comprehensive expertise in [estate planning, investment management, tax planning, etc.] To express our gratitude, we’re delighted to offer you a FREE downloadable [financial health [checklist](https://www.fppathfinder.com/members/guides/guide/what-issues-should-i-consider-when-starting-out-financially) , [budgeting template](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/152) (should uniquely speak to your niche)] to help you embark on your journey towards financial success! You will also receive our [newsletter and/or blog], which offers valuable updates, helpful resources, and exclusive content to enhance your financial journey. I'm excited to keep our connection going! Ready to start? Schedule a complimentary consultation: [insert scheduling link] Warm regards, [Your Name]

Introducing yourself and showing your commitment to their financial success builds trust and engagement. This enhances your credibility and creates a positive environment for discussing goals, which is crucial for converting leads into valued clients. Email Option: Subject: A warm message from [Your Name]. Hi [First Name], I wanted to share a quick video [insert link to website] to let you know why I’m so passionate about helping people reach their financial goals. Take a moment to watch, and I’d love to hear your thoughts. I look forward to supporting you on YOUR journey! Ready to go? [insert scheduling link] Warm regards, [Your Name]
steps.name: Personal Video Introduction
Provide a Resource (Lead Magnet)
steps.description: Lead prospects to your website whenever possible. Provide a resource or use a lead magnet (example below) to capture a prospect's email address. A lead magnet helps firms gain visibility, foster relationships, and increase sales. Email Option: Subject: More Value! Hi [Client Name], I'm excited to keep our connection going! We know that financial planning can feel overwhelming, but we're here to help you navigate it with confidence. To get started on the right foot, we invite you to explore this free resource on our website [insert link - example lead magnet below]. It’s a great way to learn more about our approach and some key considerations as you begin your financial journey. Ready to begin? [insert scheduling link] Warm regards, [Your Name] Lead Magnet Example: Get the Clarity You Need to Make Smarter Financial Decisions Feeling unsure about whether you're on track with your money? You’re not alone. That’s why I created this free resource — a simple, actionable guide that helps you get organized, understand your next steps, and feel more confident about your financial future. Inside, you’ll learn: What to focus on right now How to avoid common financial mistakes Easy steps you can take to improve your financial life When it makes sense to get professional support It’s completely free — no jargon, no overwhelm. Just practical guidance you can use today. 👉 Enter your email to get instant access.

steps.name: Addressing Common Concerns
steps.description: Addressing frequently asked questions and common concerns shows your commitment to clients' needs. This makes you a reliable resource and boosts engagement from potential clients. Email Option: Subject: Is Your Money Putting in the Same Effort You Do? Let's tackle a prevalent misconception that often hinders individuals! Many believe, “I don’t have enough to invest,” or “investing carries too much risk.” The reality is that there are customized solutions for every financial circumstance! Here’s a [blog/article] I wrote on this topic. I am here to assist you every step of the way! Here’s my link for when you’re ready to chat! [insert scheduling link] Warm regards, [Your Name]

Knowing and communicating your services helps clients understand them better and positions your offerings effectively, encouraging action when they are ready. Email Option: Subject: Discover financial planning services that align perfectly with your goals and lifestyle. We are excited to present our personalized financial planning services tailored just for you! Our expert [investment, tax planning strategies] are thoughtfully crafted to align with your unique challenges and aspirations. You can view all our services here: [insert link to website]. I am committed to equipping you with the essential tools for a successful financial journey. Are you ready to embark on this exciting path? Reach out today to schedule your complimentary consultation and begin shaping your future! [insert scheduling link] Warm regards, [Your Name]
steps.name: Deeper Dive into Services
Client Success Story (Anonymized)
steps.description: Client stories showcase real people achieving their dreams with your support. These success stories build trust, demonstrate the impact of your services, and inspire potential clients, driving engagement and conversions. Email Option: Subject: Explore how we [empowered a young family to turn their dreams into reality.] I’m excited to share an inspiring success story! We recently worked with [a wonderful young family who faced the challenge of saving for their child’s education]. Click here [insert link to website] to read more about their story and how I helped them achieve their savings goals. This is just one example of how we can together transform your financial aspirations into reality! Ready for a complimentary consultation? [insert scheduling link] Warm regards, [Your Name]

steps.description: Send an email to express appreciation for their outreach. In this [email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/411) , provide a link to your calendar to schedule a 30-minute introductory meeting (if not already scheduled), outline its purpose, and include a relevant piece of valuable 'fee-only' content. Email Option: Dear [Prospect], Thank you for reaching out to [Firm Name]. We help individuals in [niche] manage their finances and reach their goals while overcoming challenges. [I invite you to set up a 30-minute virtual meeting with me. This will give me the chance to learn more about what you want from a financial advisor.] During our meeting, I will explain the services we offer at [Firm Name]. If you think my services might be a good fit for you, we can schedule a complimentary, in-depth discovery meeting to discuss your primary life goals. I will then suggest solutions to help you achieve those goals. [If this sounds good, please pick a time on my calendar [insert link].] In the meantime, I recommend reading [this article] about how fee-only services are different from traditional brokerage firms. My priority is to put your interests first and help you live your best life. I look forward to hearing from you. Warmly, [Your Name]
steps.name: Lead Follow-Up
Send Reminder Email
steps.description: Send a [reminder email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/422) , including an agenda for the introductory meeting and a [brief questionnaire](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/420) . Remind your prospect that the meeting's purpose is to learn about each other and determine a mutual fit for working towards their goals. Email Option: Dear [Prospect], Thank you for signing up for a 30-minute introductory meeting with me on [date and time] via [a Zoom invitation]. The intent of our meeting will be for me to learn how I might be able to assist you through my guidance and a comprehensive financial plan and for you to learn about my firm and the various engagement choices I offer. Our goal at the end of this complimentary meeting will be to determine if we want to schedule a deeper dive discovery meeting, in which I can learn about the nuances of your current situation and goals. I’ll also have time to reflect on our first discussions to share some possible high-level recommendations. At the end of the meeting, we should know enough to decide whether working together makes sense. Find attached a proposed agenda for our 30-minute meeting and a [brief questionnaire](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/420) to help me know you a bit better before we meet! I look forward to meeting with you on the [Date and Time] via [Zoom]. Warm regards, [Your Name]

Connect with your prospect in person, by phone, or through video. Use this opportunity to identify their needs and goals. The insights you gather will let you customize your services and offerings to align with their objectives. Present your firm's key attributes and pricing, then propose a 'deeper dive' Discovery meeting to explore further. Use this [meeting guide](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/372) to outline the agenda and key topics. Provide a [service calendar](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/1151) to show clients your dedication to their success and that support is provided in a timely manner throughout the year. Keep the meeting to about 30 minutes, using the 80/20 Rule: spend 80% of the time listening and 20% talking. If your prospect shows interest and values your offerings, you can extend the conversation as needed. Offer to schedule a time for their Discovery meeting if they are a good fit.
steps.name: Hold Prospect Meeting

steps.description: Send an [email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/423) to thank your prospect for their time, recap the main topics discussed, and share a relevant piece of content. Confirm the date and agenda for the upcoming Discovery meeting, and include some thoughtful questions for them to consider beforehand. If the prospect was a referral, send a thank-you note to your source. Email Option: Subject: Excited for Our Next Steps Together! Hi [Client's Name], I wanted to take a moment to express my heartfelt thanks for the wonderful meeting we had recently. It was great to explore our common ground and share ideas together. As we look ahead to our next meeting, I’m really looking forward to diving deeper into your financial goals and working together to create a personalized strategy just for you. It’s going to be an exciting journey! I’ve included an [ [agenda](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/371) ] for our meeting to provide clarity on the flow of our discussion and enhance our time together. Also, take a look at this [blog I wrote on a topic they expressed interest in.] Please feel free to reach out if you have any questions or need assistance with anything. I can’t wait to continue our conversation! Warm regards, [Your Name]
steps.name: Prospect Meeting Follow-Up
Hold Discovery Meeting
steps.description: Identify your prospects' needs during this meeting. Brainstorm solutions for their main challenges and to address both short- and long-term goals. Apply the 80/20 Rule: spend 80% of the time listening and 20% talking during client conversations. Focus on understanding their needs, concerns, and goals. Use open-ended questions to encourage them to share more. This builds rapport and helps you tailor your solutions. Share relevant success stories to highlight your value. Use this agenda for [talking points](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/371) . Recap what you’ve discussed and show how you’ve supported others in similar situations. Ask if they need anything else to move forward. Aim for a verbal agreement and discuss the next steps before sending an electronic agreement for signing.

Send the follow-up information to convert your prospect into a client. Include your proposal from the meeting. Thank them for their trust and express your excitement about collaborating to achieve their goals! Encourage them to sign the agreement by a specific date so you can schedule a "Get Organized" meeting. Email Option: Dear [Client], I truly appreciate the opportunity to meet with you today! Your openness about your life goals was inspiring, and I am genuinely excited about the prospect of collaborating. I will be sending over the formal agreement for your electronic signature shortly. Once signed, we can arrange our first "Get Organized" meeting, during which I will guide you on the necessary documents to prepare. Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any questions before our meeting. Thank you for allowing me to be part of your journey toward achieving your goals! Best regards, [Your Name]

We’ll contact you shortly to gather some details about your finances and get a good understanding of your current situation. We’ll also send you a link to schedule our first meeting! Thanks again for choosing to work with me. I can’t wait for our upcoming meeting and for the great things we’ll accomplish together! [Your email signature]

steps.name: January
steps.description: This month, the focus is on cash flow and budgeting, including reviewing credit reports. Email Option: Subject: Important Topics to Start the Year! Dear [Client Name], I hope you’re having a great week! As we move into the year, we’re eager to share some intriguing topics and insights that will be the focus of our upcoming communications and activities. The first is understanding your cash flow and keeping a consistent budget. This is key towards reaching your financial goals. Regularly reviewing your income, expenses, and credit report can help you spot trends, catch potential issues early, and make confident decisions about saving and spending. If you would like assistance, wish to discuss any updates, or need some accountability to help you stay on track, please let us know. Thank you for your continued trust in us. Best regards, [email signature]

This month, the focus is on tax prep and tax return review. Email Option: Subject: Tax Preparation & Return Review Hi [Client Name], As tax season is here, I want to ensure your tax preparation goes smoothly and that we review your final return to optimize any potential tax savings. While I don't prepare taxes directly, I can coordinate with your tax preparer or assist you if you file yourself, ensuring they have all the necessary information regarding your investments and other relevant details. After your return is complete, we will review it together to identify planning opportunities, reduce future tax liability, and align your tax strategy with your long-term financial goals. Let me know if you need help gathering documents or if you’d like me to coordinate with your tax professional. Best, [Your Name]
steps.name: February

steps.description: This month, the focus is on debt management, with a review of net worth and the balance sheet. Email Option: Subject: A Quick Check-In on Your Debt & Overall Financial Picture Hi [Client Name], I'd like to check in on your debt and how it impacts your overall finances. Regularly reviewing your balance sheet and net worth help to ensure that your decisions align with your long-term goals. By examining your assets and liabilities, we can see if debt is helping you or if it is holding you back. This helps us find ways to lower interest costs, improve flexibility, and increase your net worth over time. If you have any questions or want to discuss this in detail, I’m happy to schedule some time. My goal is to make sure every part of your financial plan is aligned and moving you forward with confidence. Best regards, [Your Name]
steps.name: March
April
steps.description: This month, the focus is on preparing for the Spring Review meeting and reviewing goals. Email Option: Subject: Financial Planning Meeting Dear [Client Name], I hope you are having a wonderful week. It’s time to schedule your Spring Review meeting. During this meeting, we'll [brief description of meeting purpose or agenda]. Please upload the following items to your client portal: [portal link] [enter items needed for this meeting] Once you've uploaded those items, please complete our meeting prep form [insert link to pre-meeting prep form]. Be sure to add any additional items you wish to discuss and I will make sure we have those on the agenda. [After completing the form, you'll find a link to schedule a meeting on the confirmation page. ] Have a great week, and I look forward to seeing you. Best regards, [email signature]

This month, the focus is on insurance coverage and analysis (life, disability, home, auto, umbrella) . Email Option: Subje ct: In surance Review Hi [Client Name], I wanted to connect regarding your overall plan, focusing on your insurance coverage. My goal is to ensure these components align with your long-term aspirations. Major life milestones, such as a career change, a new addition to the family, or a move to a new home, often impact your insurance needs. These shifts are a critical time to reassess your disability, life, home, auto, and umbrella coverage to ensure your protection still aligns. If you’d like to discuss these topics or if there have been recent changes in your circumstances, I’d be happy to schedule some time with you. Thoughtful coordination can reduce risk and enhance your financial clarity! Best regards, [Your Name]
steps.name: May
June
steps.description: This month, the focus is on reviewing the estate plan, including document review (wills, trusts, POAs, advance directives), beneficiaries, and gifting strategies. Email Option: Subject: Important Touchpoint for Your Estate Planning Dear [Client Name], As we continue our planning journey together, I wanted to reconnect about your estate plan and beneficiary designations. My goal is to ensure that your documents and strategies genuinely reflect your wishes and seamlessly integrate with your overall financial plan. Let’s confirm that your beneficiary designations are up-to-date, evaluate essential documents like wills, trusts, powers of attorney, and advance healthcare directives, and explore gifting strategies that align with your aspirations and offer potential tax advantages. Whether you’ve experienced a recent life change or it has simply been a while since we last reviewed these items, now is an ideal time to ensure your coverage still aligns with your goals. Thoughtful planning in this area fosters clarity, continuity, and peace of mind for you and your loved ones. Please let us know if you’d like to have a conversation about any of these topics. Best regards, [Your Name]

steps.name: July
steps.description: This month, the focus is on retirement planning, including RMDs, Social Security, 401(k)’s & other investment accounts. Email Option: Subject: Secure Your Future with Retirement Strategies Dear [Client Name], This month, our team is focused on helping clients optimize their retirement outlook. We are looking at RMD (Required Minimum Distributions) requirements, Social Security claiming strategies, and ensuring 401(k) and other investment accounts are still on track. We are happy to discuss how we can refine these pieces of your plan. As always, please don’t hesitate to reach out if questions come up. Warmly, [Your Name]

steps.name: August
steps.description: This month, the focus is on education planning/student loans, including FAFSA reminders and savings strategies (529s, UTMAs). Email Option: Subject: Education Planning & Smart Savings Strategies Dear [Client Name], I wanted to take a moment to highlight some key areas we're focusing on this month regarding education planning and student loans: FAFSA reminders and timelines Education savings strategies, such as 529 plans and UTMAs Reviewing how education costs fit into your broader financial plan If any of these topics are timely for you or your family, I’m happy to connect and walk through your options. As always, feel free to reach out with any questions. Best regards, [Your Name]

steps.name: September
steps.description: This month, the focus is on healthcare plans, including employer benefits, Medicare planning, and FSA/HSA optimization. Email Option: Subject: A Quick Update on Your Benefits Dear [Client Name], This month’s planning focus is around employee benefits, including: Healthcare plan selection during open enrollment FSA and HSA optimization, including contribution strategies and eligible uses Medicare Planning, including enrollment timing and cost considerations If any of these topics are timely for you, especially with benefit decisions coming up, I’m happy to connect and review your options. As always, feel free to reach out with any questions. Warmly, [Your Name]

This is one of my favorite times of the year, as it gives us the opportunity to thank you for the trust you place in us and to spend time together outside of our regular meetings. Event Details: 📅 Date: [Event Date] ⏰ Time: [Event Time] 📍 Location: [Event Location or Virtual Link] We’re planning an enjoyable [brief description] with great conversation, light refreshments, and a chance to connect with other clients and our team. I hope you can join us, and I look forward to seeing you there. Warm regards, [Your Name]
steps.name: November
December
steps.description: This month, the focus is on tax planning, including charitable contributions, Roth conversions, capital gain and loss harvesting, and tax projections for the upcoming year. Email Option: Subject: Year-End Tax Planning Check-In Dear [Client Name], With year-end approaching, I’d like to check in on your tax planning and charitable giving goals. It’s a great time to make sure your donations are working effectively for both your legacy and your tax return. [For those 70½ and older, we can look into Qualified Charitable Distributions as a tax-savvy giving tool.] We can also review your portfolio for capital gains or losses and discuss whether a Roth conversion or rollover makes sense for your long-term plan. To help us get a head start, please share any updates regarding your income or retirement accounts. It’s also helpful to know about any large investment sales or estimated tax payments you’ve made recently. If a Roth conversion is on your radar, let’s chat about your current tax bracket and cash flow for any potential tax hits. We are here to help. Contact us with any questions you may have. Best, [Your Name]

steps.description: Connect with your prospect in person, by phone, or through video. Use this opportunity to identify their needs and goals. Keep the meeting to about 30 minutes, using the 80/20 Rule: spend 80% of the time listening and 20% talking. If your prospect shows interest and values your offerings, you can extend the conversation as needed. Offer to schedule a time for their Discovery meeting if they are a good fit.

Identify your prospects' needs during this meeting. Brainstorm solutions for their main challenges and to address both short- and long-term goals. Apply the 80/20 Rule: spend 80% of the time listening and 20% talking during client conversations. Focus on understanding their needs, concerns, and goals. Use open-ended questions to encourage them to share more. This builds rapport and helps you tailor your solutions. Share relevant success stories to highlight your value. Use this agenda for [talking points](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/371) . Recap what you’ve discussed and show how you’ve supported others in similar situations. Ask if they need anything else to move forward. Aim for a verbal agreement and discuss the next steps before sending an electronic agreement for signing.

The first is understanding your cash flow and keeping a consistent budget. This is key towards reaching your financial goals. Regularly reviewing your income, expenses, and credit report can help you spot trends, catch potential issues early, and make confident decisions about saving and spending. If you would like assistance, wish to discuss any updates, or need some accountability to help you stay on track, please let us know. Thank you for your continued trust in us. Best regards, [email signature]

After your return is complete, we will review it together to identify planning opportunities, reduce future tax liability, and align your tax strategy with your long-term financial goals. These shifts are a critical time to reassess your disability, life, home, auto, and umbrella coverage to ensure your protection still aligns. If you’d like to discuss these topics or if there have been recent changes in your circumstances, I’d be happy to schedule some time with you. Thoughtful coordination can reduce risk and enhance your financial clarity! Best regards, [Your Name]

Email Option: Subject: Important Touchpoint for Your Estate Planning Dear [Client Name], As we continue our planning journey together, I wanted to reconnect about your estate plan and beneficiary designations. My goal is to ensure that your documents and strategies genuinely reflect your wishes and seamlessly integrate with your overall financial plan. Let’s confirm that your beneficiary designations are up-to-date, evaluate essential documents like wills, trusts, powers of attorney, and advance healthcare directives, and explore gifting strategies that align with your aspirations and offer potential tax advantages. Whether you’ve experienced a recent life change or it has simply been a while since we last reviewed these items, now is an ideal time to ensure your coverage still aligns with your goals. Thoughtful planning in this area fosters clarity, continuity, and peace of mind for you and your loved ones. Please let us know if you’d like to have a conversation about any of these topics. Best regards, [Your Name]

We are happy to discuss how we can refine these pieces of your plan. As always, please don’t hesitate to reach out if questions come up. Warmly, [Your Name]

localAnalyses.summary:
Mailchimp and ActiveCampaign pricing assuming 2500 contacts. Levitate does not include information about the # of contacts allowed per plan tier nor their pricing. 

Given that Mailchimp has recently added SMS marketing functionality all three platforms are largely equal in this regard. Mailchimp used to offer physical postcard mailing but appears to no longer do so while Levitate appears to offer this feature in-house and ActiveCampaign partners with ClickSend. There is not currently any feature Mailchimp offers that the other two platforms do not. However, for the price, all of the features most users would want and need are included in the Standard plan at $60/month + $20/month for 1000 SMS credits while ActiveCampaign requires a bump up to enterprise at $255/month) and Levitate's pricing appears to *start* at $349/month.

ActiveCampaign offers some of the core features at a lower pricing tier compared to the other two, notably AI tools, onboarding support and behavioral targeting.

Levitate has one key distinguishing factor which is that it (appears to) offer the ability to send messages through your own Outlook or Gmail server. However, given the lack of pricing transparency and assuming that features not mentioned on the site are excluded there are some drawbacks to the system compared to the others.

steps.name: DAF Contribution - Choose Lots, Record Cost Basis and Send Paperwork to client
steps.description: Fill out "Contribute to Your Donor Advised Fund Account" form - do NOT use Schwab digital workflows for this. We have run into too many issues not being able to put in any free text for Cost Basis Info. If the funds are coming from outside of Schwab, use the "Transfer of Assets" form We need a record of when the stock was purchased (lot/aquired date) and the cost basis. On the Contribute to Your Donor Advised Fund Account form, section 2, fill out the Optional Cost Basis information. We always want to use the most appreciated shares. To find out what that is, navigate to Schwab Advisor Center, to the brokerage account, and the Cost Basis tab. In the chart, it lists all the positions in the account. Sort by the column called "% Unrealized Gain/Loss" by clicking on the cell with that title. Click twice so the arrow is pointing down (the higher percentage amounts should now be at the top). The position at top is the most appreciated in the account. Then calculate how many shares of that stock the client will need to donate to reach the dollar amount they want to donate using today's prices. Ex: If they want to donate $10k, and the current stock price is $244, you'd take 10,000/244=40.9. We always round up, go 1 share above $10k to account for market volatility, and to ensure they hit the $10k even if the price per share drops. So in this case, I would say 42 shares of whatever stock it happens to be. Fill in that amount in Section 2, and to fill in the Cost Basis Optional part in Section 2 of the form, go back to the Cost Basis tab in the Schwab Advisor center. Expand the top row, the most appreciated shares in the account, to see the Lot information. If you have enough shares in 1 lot to contribute to make the total donation amount, it's simple - use that lot, and in that same row, it will tell you the cost basis price per share. Then you have the lot date and price per share to put into the Cost Basis Optional part of the chart in Section 2 of the form. For recording purposes in WB and Holistiplan, we put "Lot date" and "(Cost basis price per share x the number of shares the client is donating)" for the cost basis amount. IF for example, you have to use multiple lots to get to your 42 shares (using our example above), then on the form, put "Use lowest cost basis" (so Schwab can calculate) and for price per share, you can use the average cost basis that is in the chart in the same row where it lists the name of the position and the symbol. For recording purposes in WB, you would say "Various Lots" for the lot and then "(Cost basis price per share x the number of shares the client is donating)" for the cost basis amount.

steps.name: DAF Contribution - Waiting on client response

steps.description: 1- Check to make sure we have their Charitable Giving Account information , either from previous years or if it's a new client, reach out to get info (see Charitable Gift Transfer LOA form for info needed) Reference for Fidelity DAFs: https://www.fidelitycharitable.org/content/dam/fc-public/docs/forms/broker-dealer-instructions.pdf For DAF Contributions, we need to capture # of shares, which position(s), acquired date, cost basis, and Fair Market Value to record in the tax letter. It's easiest to capture the acquired date and cost basis BEFORE the contribution is made, so in this step, we'll calculate all of the above and record in the tax letter right away. The last step of the workflow will be to record Fair Market Value after the contribution has been completed. 1- How to find the most appreciated shares: Sometimes Advisors will provide which lot you should use, sometimes not. Here's how to do it if you need: Navigate to Schwab Advisor Center, to the brokerage account, and the Cost Basis tab. In the chart, it lists all the positions in the account. Sort by the column called "% Unrealized Gain/Loss" by clicking on the cell with that title. Click twice so the arrow is pointing down (the higher percentage amounts should now be at the top). The position at top is the most appreciated in the account. 2 - Then calculate how many shares of that stock the client will need to donate to reach the dollar amount they want to donate using today's prices. Ex: If they want to donate $10k, and the current stock price is $244, you'd take 10,000/244=40.9. We always round up, go 1 share above $10k to account for market volatility, and to ensure they hit the $10k even if the price per share drops. So in this case, I would say 42 shares of whatever stock it happens to be. 3 - To get the Cost Basis , go back to the Cost Basis tab in the Schwab Advisor center. Expand the top row, the most appreciated shares in the account, to see the Lot information. If you have enough shares in 1 lot to contribute to make the total donation amount, it's simple - use that lot, and in that same row, it will tell you the cost basis price per share. Then you have the lot date (to enter into Move Money tab) and price per share (to record for later). For recording purposes in the tax letter, we put "Lot date" and "(Cost basis price per share x the number of shares the client is donating)" for the cost basis amount as a comment in this step. IF for example, you have to use multiple lots to get to your 42 shares (using our example above), for price per share, you can use the average cost basis that is in the chart in the same row where it lists the name of the position and the symbol. For recording purposes in WB, you would say "Various Lots" for the lot and then "(Cost basis price per share x the number of shares the client is donating)" for the cost basis amount. 4 - Prepare the Charitable Gift Transfer LOA form via DocuSign: Use the information you calculated above to put on the form. Be sure to specify which lots. If the client is donating a position / positions that are going to require a ton of different lots, you can just say "Use lowest cost basis" in the field that asks for the lot. 5- Put the position/# of shares/cost basis information in the tax letter now. You will get Fair Market Value after the contribution is completed. Go to client tax letter, select 2026 or create new tax letter for 2026 Add the (+Gave to a Donor Advised Fund) section, if not added already Date = Date of donation Description = (# of) shares of (position), acquired on (date) (if various lots, just say "various lots"), cost basis ($ original purchase price x # of shares)

steps.name: DAF Contribution Bunched - 2nd Tranche - (Outside of Schwab) Choose Lots and Prepare Charitable Gift Transfer LOA form
steps.description: 1- Check to make sure we have their Charitable Giving Account information , either from previous years or if it's a new client, reach out to get info (see Charitable Gift Transfer LOA form for info needed) Reference for Fidelity DAFs: https://www.fidelitycharitable.org/content/dam/fc-public/docs/forms/broker-dealer-instructions.pdf For DAF Contributions, we need to capture # of shares, which position(s), acquired date, cost basis, and Fair Market Value to record in the tax letter. It's easiest to capture the acquired date and cost basis BEFORE the contribution is made, so in this step, we'll calculate all of the above and record in the tax letter right away. The last step of the workflow will be to record Fair Market Value after the contribution has been completed. 1- How to find the most appreciated shares: Sometimes Advisors will provide which lot you should use, sometimes not. Here's how to do it if you need: Navigate to Schwab Advisor Center, to the brokerage account, and the Cost Basis tab. In the chart, it lists all the positions in the account. Sort by the column called "% Unrealized Gain/Loss" by clicking on the cell with that title. Click twice so the arrow is pointing down (the higher percentage amounts should now be at the top). The position at top is the most appreciated in the account. 2 - Then calculate how many shares of that stock the client will need to donate to reach the dollar amount they want to donate using today's prices. Ex: If they want to donate $10k, and the current stock price is $244, you'd take 10,000/244=40.9. We always round up, go 1 share above $10k to account for market volatility, and to ensure they hit the $10k even if the price per share drops. So in this case, I would say 42 shares of whatever stock it happens to be. 3 - To get the Cost Basis , go back to the Cost Basis tab in the Schwab Advisor center. Expand the top row, the most appreciated shares in the account, to see the Lot information. If you have enough shares in 1 lot to contribute to make the total donation amount, it's simple - use that lot, and in that same row, it will tell you the cost basis price per share. Then you have the lot date (to enter into Move Money tab) and price per share (to record for later). For recording purposes in the tax letter, we put "Lot date" and "(Cost basis price per share x the number of shares the client is donating)" for the cost basis amount as a comment in this step. IF for example, you have to use multiple lots to get to your 42 shares (using our example above), for price per share, you can use the average cost basis that is in the chart in the same row where it lists the name of the position and the symbol. For recording purposes in WB, you would say "Various Lots" for the lot and then "(Cost basis price per share x the number of shares the client is donating)" for the cost basis amount. 4 - Prepare the Charitable Gift Transfer LOA form via DocuSign: Use the information you calculated above to put on the form. Be sure to specify which lots. If the client is donating a position / positions that are going to require a ton of different lots, you can just say "Use lowest cost basis" in the field that asks for the lot. 5- Put the position/# of shares/cost basis information in the tax letter now. You will get Fair Market Value after the contribution is completed. Go to client tax letter, select 2026 or create new tax letter for 2026 Add the (+Gave to a Donor Advised Fund) section, if not added already Date = Date of donation Description = (# of) shares of (position), acquired on (date) (if various lots, just say "various lots"), cost basis ($ original purchase price x # of shares)

Switching from Microsoft to Google is fairly intuitive, but there are also a few nuances that can be helpful as you navigate the transition. Here’s a few trainings and resources to help you get up to speed. These aren’t required, but we’ll check-in to see how it’s going and if you need any support: The [Google Workspace Learning Center](https://support.google.com/a/users/?hl=en&sjid=13362379873811356199-NC#topic=9247638) is a great resource for you to do some self-training to get up to speed. You’ll likely find the links below most helpful, but if you’re not sure where to start just ask for help. Our Most Used Tools within Google [Google Docs](https://support.google.com/a/users/answer/9282664?visit_id=638594316267912944-1135560859&hl=en&rd=1) [Googel Calendar ](https://support.google.com/a/users/answer/9247501?visit_id=638594316267912944-1135560859&hl=en&rd=1) [Google Drive](https://support.google.com/a/users/answer/9282958?visit_id=638594316267912944-1135560859&hl=en&rd=1) [Google Sheets](https://support.google.com/a/users/answer/9282959?visit_id=638594316267912944-1135560859&hl=en&rd=1) Coming from Microsoft and Want to Understand the Differences: [Switch from Microsoft to Google Workspace](https://support.google.com/a/users/answer/9247553?visit_id=638594316267912944-1135560859&hl=en&rd=1) Be sure to review the assigned [File Saving & Naming SOP](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rwesEEoUbFhiN8xYq9lVLQqeOjosZ_qfG1amBZS7VHQ/edit?usp=drive_link) training as it helps provide guidelines for how to create new docs and where to save them. Finally, a few things to know about how we use Google: We rarely save a document as a new version or with a new name, Google’s version history handles that for us and saves as you go. If you want others to see your changes, be sure to change the setting (its teh little pencil icon) to Suggestions. This is the same as Track Changes in Microsoft. Start new documents from the folder you want them saved! Creating a new doc will automatically save it to your My Drive, which limits who can have access. By saving items in the correct drive, you can ensure that the team has access and new employees don't need to request access to indv. docs. More than one person can be in a doc and editing it at the same time.
