For those who want to set up Autopay, here's how: To get one annoying task off your plate this year, I wanted to share the steps for enrolling in autopay for your VAF fee: Steps to Set-Up Autopay 1) Register an account for this email address, using this link: https://app-wf.autobooks.co/SMB/Guest/Register.aspx 2) Login using the same email address and the password you just established, using this link: https://app-wf.autobooks.co/sign_in.aspx 3) Once you've logged in, click the blue "Change My Autopay Preferences" button on the right side of the screen. 4) Click "+ Add Payment Options" in the upper right corner of the screen 5) Enter the information for your bank account and then hit continue. 6) Check the "Autopay" checkbox and then click the blue "Save Preferences" Button. This will ensure your invoices are paid automatically 7) Pay any currently due invoices now, since autopay won't apply to those.

steps.description: Email template: Hi (Client), Unfortunately for retirement plans, we can’t just submit a normal transfer form to the other custodian from Schwab, like we would with any other Brokerage/IRA account. For these types of plans, the Rollover Request has to come from the account holder. So, you would need to call Fidelity (the number should be on your 401k statement) and tell them “I want to initiate a Rollover of my account TO my Schwab Individual 401k." A couple of things to note before calling… (a) you might want to have your Schwab Individual 401k account number and title handy. So just log into Schwab Alliance, where you can view the account and full account number before calling. (b) Sometimes all they need is just a verbal request from the account holder to complete the rollover and other times, they’ll require paperwork. If there’s paperwork that needs to be filled out, I am happy to fill out any of their paperwork on your behalf to get these rollovers initiated! (c) Usually the process is they will mail a check out to you and then you will mail it to Schwab to be deposited within 60 days of the check date. They'll likely ask you how the check should be written -- the payee should be "Charles Schwab & Co., Inc. FBO (Name on your account)". Ideally, they would include your full 8-digit Schwab IRA account number on the memo line (it's the account ending xxx), but sometimes their software doesn't allow for that. If that's the case, you can just write the full account number in the memo area of the check when you receive it in the mail. Also, you will not sign the check when you receive it. You'll need to mail it to Schwab unsigned, because Schwab will stamp it when they make the deposit. Once you have the check in hand, you can mail it to Schwab at: Charles Schwab & Co., INC P.O. Box 2380 Omaha, NE 68103 I believe that’s all! Let me know if you have any questions and please keep us posted once you speak with them.

Reach out today to schedule your complimentary consultation and begin shaping your future! [insert scheduling link] Warm regards, [Your Name]

steps.description: Client stories showcase real people achieving their dreams with your support. These success stories build trust, demonstrate the impact of your services, and inspire potential clients, driving engagement and conversions. Email Option: Subject: Explore how we [empowered a young family to turn their dreams into reality.] I’m excited to share an inspiring success story! We recently worked with [a wonderful young family who faced the challenge of saving for their child’s education]. Click here [insert link to website] to read more about their story and how I helped them achieve their savings goals. This is just one example of how we can together transform your financial aspirations into reality! Ready for a complimentary consultation? [insert scheduling link] Warm regards, [Your Name]

Send an email to express appreciation for their outreach. In this [email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/411) , provide a link to your calendar to schedule a 30-minute introductory meeting (if not already scheduled), outline its purpose, and include a relevant piece of valuable 'fee-only' content. Email Option: Dear [Prospect], Thank you for reaching out to [Firm Name]. We help individuals in [niche] manage their finances and reach their goals while overcoming challenges. [I invite you to set up a 30-minute virtual meeting with me. This will give me the chance to learn more about what you want from a financial advisor.] During our meeting, I will explain the services we offer at [Firm Name]. If you think my services might be a good fit for you, we can schedule a complimentary, in-depth discovery meeting to discuss your primary life goals. I will then suggest solutions to help you achieve those goals. [If this sounds good, please pick a time on my calendar [insert link].] In the meantime, I recommend reading [this article] about how fee-only services are different from traditional brokerage firms. My priority is to put your interests first and help you live your best life. I look forward to hearing from you. Warmly, [Your Name]
steps.name: Lead Follow-Up
Send Reminder Email
steps.description: Send a [reminder email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/422) , including an agenda for the introductory meeting and a [brief questionnaire](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/420) . Remind your prospect that the meeting's purpose is to learn about each other and determine a mutual fit for working towards their goals. Email Option: Dear [Prospect], Thank you for signing up for a 30-minute introductory meeting with me on [date and time] via [a Zoom invitation]. The intent of our meeting will be for me to learn how I might be able to assist you through my guidance and a comprehensive financial plan and for you to learn about my firm and the various engagement choices I offer. Our goal at the end of this complimentary meeting will be to determine if we want to schedule a deeper dive discovery meeting, in which I can learn about the nuances of your current situation and goals. I’ll also have time to reflect on our first discussions to share some possible high-level recommendations. At the end of the meeting, we should know enough to decide whether working together makes sense. Find attached a proposed agenda for our 30-minute meeting and a [brief questionnaire](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/420) to help me know you a bit better before we meet! I look forward to meeting with you on the [Date and Time] via [Zoom]. Warm regards, [Your Name]

steps.name: Hold Prospect Meeting
steps.description: Connect with your prospect in person, by phone, or through video. Use this opportunity to identify their needs and goals. The insights you gather will let you customize your services and offerings to align with their objectives. Present your firm's key attributes and pricing, then propose a 'deeper dive' Discovery meeting to explore further. Use this [meeting guide](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/372) to outline the agenda and key topics. Provide a [service calendar](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/1151) to show clients your dedication to their success and that support is provided in a timely manner throughout the year. Keep the meeting to about 30 minutes, using the 80/20 Rule: spend 80% of the time listening and 20% talking. If your prospect shows interest and values your offerings, you can extend the conversation as needed. Offer to schedule a time for their Discovery meeting if they are a good fit.

steps.name: Prospect Meeting Follow-Up
steps.description: Send an [email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/423) to thank your prospect for their time, recap the main topics discussed, and share a relevant piece of content. Confirm the date and agenda for the upcoming Discovery meeting, and include some thoughtful questions for them to consider beforehand. If the prospect was a referral, send a thank-you note to your source. Email Option: Subject: Excited for Our Next Steps Together! Hi [Client's Name], I wanted to take a moment to express my heartfelt thanks for the wonderful meeting we had recently. It was great to explore our common ground and share ideas together. As we look ahead to our next meeting, I’m really looking forward to diving deeper into your financial goals and working together to create a personalized strategy just for you. It’s going to be an exciting journey! I’ve included an [ [agenda](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/371) ] for our meeting to provide clarity on the flow of our discussion and enhance our time together. Also, take a look at this [blog I wrote on a topic they expressed interest in.] Please feel free to reach out if you have any questions or need assistance with anything. I can’t wait to continue our conversation! Warm regards, [Your Name]

Identify your prospects' needs during this meeting. Brainstorm solutions for their main challenges and to address both short- and long-term goals. Apply the 80/20 Rule: spend 80% of the time listening and 20% talking during client conversations. Focus on understanding their needs, concerns, and goals. Use open-ended questions to encourage them to share more. This builds rapport and helps you tailor your solutions. Share relevant success stories to highlight your value. Use this agenda for [talking points](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/371) . Recap what you’ve discussed and show how you’ve supported others in similar situations. Ask if they need anything else to move forward. Aim for a verbal agreement and discuss the next steps before sending an electronic agreement for signing.

steps.name: January
steps.description: This month, the focus is on cash flow and budgeting, including reviewing credit reports. Email Option: Subject: Important Topics to Start the Year! Dear [Client Name], I hope you’re having a great week! As we move into the year, we’re eager to share some intriguing topics and insights that will be the focus of our upcoming communications and activities. The first is understanding your cash flow and keeping a consistent budget. This is key towards reaching your financial goals. Regularly reviewing your income, expenses, and credit report can help you spot trends, catch potential issues early, and make confident decisions about saving and spending. If you would like assistance, wish to discuss any updates, or need some accountability to help you stay on track, please let us know. Thank you for your continued trust in us. Best regards, [email signature]

steps.name: February
steps.description: This month, the focus is on tax prep and tax return review. Email Option: Subject: Tax Preparation & Return Review Hi [Client Name], As tax season is here, I want to ensure your tax preparation goes smoothly and that we review your final return to optimize any potential tax savings. While I don't prepare taxes directly, I can coordinate with your tax preparer or assist you if you file yourself, ensuring they have all the necessary information regarding your investments and other relevant details. After your return is complete, we will review it together to identify planning opportunities, reduce future tax liability, and align your tax strategy with your long-term financial goals. Let me know if you need help gathering documents or if you’d like me to coordinate with your tax professional. Best, [Your Name]

This month, the focus is on debt management, with a review of net worth and the balance sheet. Email Option: Subject: A Quick Check-In on Your Debt & Overall Financial Picture Hi [Client Name], I'd like to check in on your debt and how it impacts your overall finances. Regularly reviewing your balance sheet and net worth help to ensure that your decisions align with your long-term goals. By examining your assets and liabilities, we can see if debt is helping you or if it is holding you back. This helps us find ways to lower interest costs, improve flexibility, and increase your net worth over time. If you have any questions or want to discuss this in detail, I’m happy to schedule some time. My goal is to make sure every part of your financial plan is aligned and moving you forward with confidence. Best regards, [Your Name]
steps.name: March

steps.description: This month, the focus is on preparing for the Spring Review meeting and reviewing goals. steps.description: This month, the focus is on insurance coverage and analysis (life, disability, home, auto, umbrella) . Email Option: Subje ct: In surance Review Hi [Client Name], I wanted to connect regarding your overall plan, focusing on your insurance coverage. My goal is to ensure these components align with your long-term aspirations. Major life milestones, such as a career change, a new addition to the family, or a move to a new home, often impact your insurance needs. These shifts are a critical time to reassess your disability, life, home, auto, and umbrella coverage to ensure your protection still aligns. If you’d like to discuss these topics or if there have been recent changes in your circumstances, I’d be happy to schedule some time with you. Thoughtful coordination can reduce risk and enhance your financial clarity! Best regards, [Your Name]

steps.name: June
steps.description: This month, the focus is on reviewing the estate plan, including document review (wills, trusts, POAs, advance directives), beneficiaries, and gifting strategies. Email Option: Subject: Important Touchpoint for Your Estate Planning Dear [Client Name], As we continue our planning journey together, I wanted to reconnect about your estate plan and beneficiary designations. My goal is to ensure that your documents and strategies genuinely reflect your wishes and seamlessly integrate with your overall financial plan. Let’s confirm that your beneficiary designations are up-to-date, evaluate essential documents like wills, trusts, powers of attorney, and advance healthcare directives, and explore gifting strategies that align with your aspirations and offer potential tax advantages. Whether you’ve experienced a recent life change or it has simply been a while since we last reviewed these items, now is an ideal time to ensure your coverage still aligns with your goals. Thoughtful planning in this area fosters clarity, continuity, and peace of mind for you and your loved ones. Please let us know if you’d like to have a conversation about any of these topics. Best regards, [Your Name]

steps.name: July
steps.description: This month, the focus is on retirement planning, including RMDs, Social Security, 401(k)’s & other investment accounts. Email Option: Subject: Secure Your Future with Retirement Strategies Dear [Client Name], This month, our team is focused on helping clients optimize their retirement outlook. We are looking at RMD (Required Minimum Distributions) requirements, Social Security claiming strategies, and ensuring 401(k) and other investment accounts are still on track. We are happy to discuss how we can refine these pieces of your plan. As always, please don’t hesitate to reach out if questions come up. Warmly, [Your Name]

steps.name: August
steps.description: This month, the focus is on education planning/student loans, including FAFSA reminders and savings strategies (529s, UTMAs). Email Option: Subject: Education Planning & Smart Savings Strategies Dear [Client Name], I wanted to take a moment to highlight some key areas we're focusing on this month regarding education planning and student loans: FAFSA reminders and timelines Education savings strategies, such as 529 plans and UTMAs Reviewing how education costs fit into your broader financial plan If any of these topics are timely for you or your family, I’m happy to connect and walk through your options. As always, feel free to reach out with any questions. Best regards, [Your Name]

steps.name: September
steps.description: This month, the focus is on healthcare plans, including employer benefits, Medicare planning, and FSA/HSA optimization. I hope you can join us, and I look forward to seeing you there. Warm regards, [Your Name]

This month, the focus is on tax planning, including charitable contributions, Roth conversions, capital gain and loss harvesting, and tax projections for the upcoming year. Email Option: Subject: Year-End Tax Planning Check-In Dear [Client Name], With year-end approaching, I’d like to check in on your tax planning and charitable giving goals. It’s a great time to make sure your donations are working effectively for both your legacy and your tax return. [For those 70½ and older, we can look into Qualified Charitable Distributions as a tax-savvy giving tool.] We can also review your portfolio for capital gains or losses and discuss whether a Roth conversion or rollover makes sense for your long-term plan. To help us get a head start, please share any updates regarding your income or retirement accounts. It’s also helpful to know about any large investment sales or estimated tax payments you’ve made recently. If a Roth conversion is on your radar, let’s chat about your current tax bracket and cash flow for any potential tax hits. We are here to help. Contact us with any questions you may have. It allows prospects to receive regular updates, valuable resources, and exclusive content, improving their overall experience. Email Option: Your Path to Financial Confidence Starts Here! Hello, and welcome! It’s great to connect with you! I want to introduce myself and my team at [Firm Name]. We are excited to have you in our community. We are committed to empowering individuals like you through our comprehensive expertise in [estate planning, investment management, tax planning, etc.] To express our gratitude, we’re delighted to offer you a FREE downloadable [financial health [checklist](https://www.fppathfinder.com/members/guides/guide/what-issues-should-i-consider-when-starting-out-financially) , [budgeting template](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/152) (should uniquely speak to your niche)] to help you embark on your journey towards financial success! You will also receive our [newsletter and/or blog], which offers valuable updates, helpful resources, and exclusive content to enhance your financial journey. I'm excited to keep our connection going! Ready to start? Schedule a complimentary consultation: [insert scheduling link] Warm regards, [Your Name]

steps.description: Introducing yourself and showing your commitment to their financial success builds trust and engagement. Email Option: Subject: A warm message from [Your Name]. Hi [First Name], I wanted to share a quick video [insert link to website] to let you know why I’m so passionate about helping people reach their financial goals. Take a moment to watch, and I’d love to hear your thoughts. I look forward to supporting you on YOUR journey! Ready to go? [insert scheduling link] Warm regards, [Your Name]

Provide a Resource (Lead Magnet)
steps.description: Lead prospects to your website whenever possible. Provide a resource or use a lead magnet (example below) to capture a prospect's email address. A lead magnet helps firms gain visibility, foster relationships, and increase sales. Email Option: Subject: More Value! Hi [Client Name], I'm excited to keep our connection going! We know that financial planning can feel overwhelming, but we're here to help you navigate it with confidence. To get started on the right foot, we invite you to explore this free resource on our website [insert link - example lead magnet below]. It’s a great way to learn more about our approach and some key considerations as you begin your financial journey. Ready to begin? [insert scheduling link] Warm regards, [Your Name] Lead Magnet Example: Get the Clarity You Need to Make Smarter Financial Decisions Feeling unsure about whether you're on track with your money? You’re not alone. That’s why I created this free resource — a simple, actionable guide that helps you get organized, understand your next steps, and feel more confident about your financial future. Inside, you’ll learn: What to focus on right now How to avoid common financial mistakes Easy steps you can take to improve your financial life When it makes sense to get professional support It’s completely free — no jargon, no overwhelm. Just practical guidance you can use today. 👉 Enter your email to get instant access.

steps.name: Lead Follow-Up
steps.description: Send an email to express appreciation for their outreach. In this [email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/411) , provide a link to your calendar to schedule a 30-minute introductory meeting (if not already scheduled), outline its purpose, and include a relevant piece of valuable 'fee-only' content. Email Option: Dear [Prospect], Thank you for reaching out to [Firm Name]. We help individuals in [niche] manage their finances and reach their goals while overcoming challenges. [I invite you to set up a 30-minute virtual meeting with me. This will give me the chance to learn more about what you want from a financial advisor.] During our meeting, I will explain the services we offer at [Firm Name]. If you think my services might be a good fit for you, we can schedule a complimentary, in-depth discovery meeting to discuss your primary life goals. I will then suggest solutions to help you achieve those goals. [If this sounds good, please pick a time on my calendar [insert link].] In the meantime, I recommend reading [this article] about how fee-only services are different from traditional brokerage firms. My priority is to put your interests first and help you live your best life. I look forward to hearing from you. Warmly, [Your Name]

steps.name: Send Reminder Email
steps.description: Send a [reminder email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/422) , including an agenda for the introductory meeting and a [brief questionnaire](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/420) . Remind your prospect that the meeting's purpose is to learn about each other and determine a mutual fit for working towards their goals. Email Option: Dear [Prospect], Thank you for signing up for a 30-minute introductory meeting with me on [date and time] via [a Zoom invitation]. The intent of our meeting will be for me to learn how I might be able to assist you through my guidance and a comprehensive financial plan and for you to learn about my firm and the various engagement choices I offer. Our goal at the end of this complimentary meeting will be to determine if we want to schedule a deeper dive discovery meeting, in which I can learn about the nuances of your current situation and goals. I’ll also have time to reflect on our first discussions to share some possible high-level recommendations. At the end of the meeting, we should know enough to decide whether working together makes sense. Find attached a proposed agenda for our 30-minute meeting and a [brief questionnaire](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/420) to help me know you a bit better before we meet! I look forward to meeting with you on the [Date and Time] via [Zoom]. Warm regards, [Your Name]

Connect with your prospect in person, by phone, or through video. Use this opportunity to identify their needs and goals. The insights you gather will let you customize your services and offerings to align with their objectives. Present your firm's key attributes and pricing, then propose a 'deeper dive' Discovery meeting to explore further. Use this [meeting guide](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/372) to outline the agenda and key topics. Provide a [service calendar](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/1151) to show clients your dedication to their success and that support is provided in a timely manner throughout the year. Keep the meeting to about 30 minutes, using the 80/20 Rule: spend 80% of the time listening and 20% talking. If your prospect shows interest and values your offerings, you can extend the conversation as needed. Offer to schedule a time for their Discovery meeting if they are a good fit.
steps.name: Hold Prospect Meeting

steps.description: Send an [email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/423) to thank your prospect for their time, recap the main topics discussed, and share a relevant piece of content. Confirm the date and agenda for the upcoming Discovery meeting, and include some thoughtful questions for them to consider beforehand. If the prospect was a referral, send a thank-you note to your source. Email Option: Subject: Excited for Our Next Steps Together! Hi [Client's Name], I wanted to take a moment to express my heartfelt thanks for the wonderful meeting we had recently. It was great to explore our common ground and share ideas together. As we look ahead to our next meeting, I’m really looking forward to diving deeper into your financial goals and working together to create a personalized strategy just for you. It’s going to be an exciting journey! I’ve included an [ [agenda](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/371) ] for our meeting to provide clarity on the flow of our discussion and enhance our time together. Also, take a look at this [blog I wrote on a topic they expressed interest in.] Please feel free to reach out if you have any questions or need assistance with anything. I can’t wait to continue our conversation! Warm regards, [Your Name]
steps.name: Prospect Meeting Follow-Up

steps.description: Identify your prospects' needs during this meeting. Brainstorm solutions for their main challenges and to address both short- and long-term goals. Apply the 80/20 Rule: spend 80% of the time listening and 20% talking during client conversations. Focus on understanding their needs, concerns, and goals. Use open-ended questions to encourage them to share more. This builds rapport and helps you tailor your solutions. Share relevant success stories to highlight your value. Use this agenda for [talking points](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/371) . Recap what you’ve discussed and show how you’ve supported others in similar situations. Ask if they need anything else to move forward. Aim for a verbal agreement and discuss the next steps before sending an electronic agreement for signing.

Once signed, we can arrange our first "Get Organized" meeting, during which I will guide you on the necessary documents to prepare. Email Option: Hey [Client Name] , Welcome to [Firm Name]! I’m really excited to kick off this planning journey with you, and I want to say a big thank you for trusting me to help you out. My goal is to make sure all your needs and dreams are taken care of every step of the way as we work together. Let’s chat about what’s coming up next. In your welcome packet, you’ll find our annual service calendar. It’s packed with information about when we’ll tackle different parts of your financial life. You’ll also get our Client Engagement document, which lays out what you can expect from me. I’ll include a copy of your contract along with the Form ADV that has all the important legal details. Soon, you’ll receive your login information for the Client Portal and Payment Profile. This secure access will make it easy for you to update your financial information privately. We’ll contact you shortly to gather some details about your finances and get a good understanding of your current situation. We’ll also send you a link to schedule our first meeting! Thanks again for choosing to work with me. I can’t wait for our upcoming meeting and for the great things we’ll accomplish together! [Your email signature]

The next step in our process is a “Get Organized” meeting, where we’ll gather and organize your financial information, confirm key details, and make sure everything is set up securely to support your ongoing planning. This meeting typically lasts about 90 minutes. You can schedule at a time that works best for you using this link: [schedule meeting link] Once your meeting is scheduled, I’ll share [instructions and a checklist] to help you prepare. Don’t worry if you don’t have everything ready, we’ll work through it together. Please feel free to reach out if you have any questions in the meantime. I’m looking forward to continuing our work together. Warmly, [Your Name]

steps.name: January
steps.description: This month, the focus is on cash flow and budgeting, including reviewing credit reports. Email Option: Subject: Important Topics to Start the Year! Dear [Client Name], I hope you’re having a great week! As we move into the year, we’re eager to share some intriguing topics and insights that will be the focus of our upcoming communications and activities. The first is understanding your cash flow and keeping a consistent budget. This is key towards reaching your financial goals. Regularly reviewing your income, expenses, and credit report can help you spot trends, catch potential issues early, and make confident decisions about saving and spending. If you would like assistance, wish to discuss any updates, or need some accountability to help you stay on track, please let us know. Thank you for your continued trust in us. Best regards, [email signature]

steps.name: February
steps.description: This month, the focus is on tax prep and tax return review. Email Option: Subject: Tax Preparation & Return Review Hi [Client Name], As tax season is here, I want to ensure your tax preparation goes smoothly and that we review your final return to optimize any potential tax savings. While I don't prepare taxes directly, I can coordinate with your tax preparer or assist you if you file yourself, ensuring they have all the necessary information regarding your investments and other relevant details. After your return is complete, we will review it together to identify planning opportunities, reduce future tax liability, and align your tax strategy with your long-term financial goals. Let me know if you need help gathering documents or if you’d like me to coordinate with your tax professional. Best, [Your Name]

steps.name: March
steps.description: This month, the focus is on debt management, with a review of net worth and the balance sheet. Email Option: Subject: A Quick Check-In on Your Debt & Overall Financial Picture Hi [Client Name], I'd like to check in on your debt and how it impacts your overall finances. Regularly reviewing your balance sheet and net worth help to ensure that your decisions align with your long-term goals. By examining your assets and liabilities, we can see if debt is helping you or if it is holding you back. This helps us find ways to lower interest costs, improve flexibility, and increase your net worth over time. If you have any questions or want to discuss this in detail, I’m happy to schedule some time. My goal is to make sure every part of your financial plan is aligned and moving you forward with confidence. Best regards, [Your Name]

This month, the focus is on preparing for the Spring Review meeting and reviewing goals. Email Option: Subject: Financial Planning Meeting Dear [Client Name], I hope you are having a wonderful week. It’s time to schedule your Spring Review meeting. During this meeting, we'll [brief description of meeting purpose or agenda]. Please upload the following items to your client portal: [portal link] [enter items needed for this meeting] Once you've uploaded those items, please complete our meeting prep form [insert link to pre-meeting prep form]. Be sure to add any additional items you wish to discuss and I will make sure we have those on the agenda. [After completing the form, you'll find a link to schedule a meeting on the confirmation page. ] Have a great week, and I look forward to seeing you. Best regards, [email signature]
steps.name: April

steps.description: This month, the focus is on insurance coverage and analysis (life, disability, home, auto, umbrella) . Email Option: Subje ct: In surance Review Hi [Client Name], I wanted to connect regarding your overall plan, focusing on your insurance coverage. My goal is to ensure these components align with your long-term aspirations. Major life milestones, such as a career change, a new addition to the family, or a move to a new home, often impact your insurance needs. These shifts are a critical time to reassess your disability, life, home, auto, and umbrella coverage to ensure your protection still aligns. If you’d like to discuss these topics or if there have been recent changes in your circumstances, I’d be happy to schedule some time with you. Thoughtful coordination can reduce risk and enhance your financial clarity! Best regards, [Your Name]
steps.name: May

steps.description: This month, the focus is on reviewing the estate plan, including document review (wills, trusts, POAs, advance directives), beneficiaries, and gifting strategies. Email Option: Subject: Important Touchpoint for Your Estate Planning Dear [Client Name], As we continue our planning journey together, I wanted to reconnect about your estate plan and beneficiary designations. My goal is to ensure that your documents and strategies genuinely reflect your wishes and seamlessly integrate with your overall financial plan. Let’s confirm that your beneficiary designations are up-to-date, evaluate essential documents like wills, trusts, powers of attorney, and advance healthcare directives, and explore gifting strategies that align with your aspirations and offer potential tax advantages. Whether you’ve experienced a recent life change or it has simply been a while since we last reviewed these items, now is an ideal time to ensure your coverage still aligns with your goals. Thoughtful planning in this area fosters clarity, continuity, and peace of mind for you and your loved ones. Please let us know if you’d like to have a conversation about any of these topics. Best regards, [Your Name]
steps.name: June

steps.description: This month, the focus is on retirement planning, including RMDs, Social Security, 401(k)’s & other investment accounts. Email Option: Subject: Secure Your Future with Retirement Strategies Dear [Client Name], This month, our team is focused on helping clients optimize their retirement outlook. We are looking at RMD (Required Minimum Distributions) requirements, Social Security claiming strategies, and ensuring 401(k) and other investment accounts are still on track. We are happy to discuss how we can refine these pieces of your plan. As always, please don’t hesitate to reach out if questions come up. Warmly, [Your Name]
steps.name: July
August
steps.description: This month, the focus is on education planning/student loans, including FAFSA reminders and savings strategies (529s, UTMAs). Email Option: Subject: Education Planning & Smart Savings Strategies Dear [Client Name], I wanted to take a moment to highlight some key areas we're focusing on this month regarding education planning and student loans: FAFSA reminders and timelines Education savings strategies, such as 529 plans and UTMAs Reviewing how education costs fit into your broader financial plan If any of these topics are timely for you or your family, I’m happy to connect and walk through your options. As always, feel free to reach out with any questions. Best regards, [Your Name]

This month, the focus is on healthcare plans, including employer benefits, Medicare planning, and FSA/HSA optimization. Email Option: Subject: A Quick Update on Your Benefits Dear [Client Name], This month’s planning focus is around employee benefits, including: Healthcare plan selection during open enrollment FSA and HSA optimization, including contribution strategies and eligible uses Medicare Planning, including enrollment timing and cost considerations If any of these topics are timely for you, especially with benefit decisions coming up, I’m happy to connect and review your options. As always, feel free to reach out with any questions. Warmly, [Your Name]
steps.name: September

steps.description: This month, the focus is on the Fall Review eeting. Subject: Your Fall Planning Review Dear [Client Name], It’s time to schedule your Fall Review meeting. During this meeting, we'll [brief description of meeting purpose or agenda]. Please upload the following items to your client portal: [portal link] [enter items needed for this meeting] Once you've uploaded those items, please complete our meeting prep form [insert link to pre-meeting prep form]. Be sure to add any additional items you wish to discuss and I will make sure we have those on the agenda. steps.name: October

steps.description: This month's focus is the Client Appreciation Event. This event should help build loyalty, trust, and strong, long-term relationships. Subject: You’re Invited: Our Thank You to You Dear [Client Name], I’m excited to invite you to our Annual Client Appreciation Event! This is one of my favorite times of the year, as it gives us the opportunity to thank you for the trust you place in us and to spend time together outside of our regular meetings. Event Details: 📅 Date: [Event Date] ⏰ Time: [Event Time] 📍 Location: [Event Location or Virtual Link] We’re planning an enjoyable [brief description] with great conversation, light refreshments, and a chance to connect with other clients and our team. Feel free to bring a guest; we’d love to meet the people who matter most to you. Please let us know if you’re able to attend by [RSVP Date]. You can RSVP here: [RSVP or Registration Link]. I hope you can join us, and I look forward to seeing you there. Warm regards, [Your Name]
steps.name: November
December
steps.description: This month, the focus is on tax planning, including charitable contributions, Roth conversions, capital gain and loss harvesting, and tax projections for the upcoming year. Email Option: Subject: Year-End Tax Planning Check-In Dear [Client Name], With year-end approaching, I’d like to check in on your tax planning and charitable giving goals. It’s a great time to make sure your donations are working effectively for both your legacy and your tax return. [For those 70½ and older, we can look into Qualified Charitable Distributions as a tax-savvy giving tool.] We can also review your portfolio for capital gains or losses and discuss whether a Roth conversion or rollover makes sense for your long-term plan. To help us get a head start, please share any updates regarding your income or retirement accounts. It’s also helpful to know about any large investment sales or estimated tax payments you’ve made recently. If a Roth conversion is on your radar, let’s chat about your current tax bracket and cash flow for any potential tax hits. We are here to help. Contact us with any questions you may have. Best, [Your Name]

steps.description: Send an email to express appreciation for their outreach. In this [email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/411) , provide a link to your calendar to schedule a 30-minute introductory meeting (if not already scheduled), outline its purpose, and include a relevant piece of valuable 'fee-only' content. Email Option: Dear [Prospect], Thank you for reaching out to [Firm Name]. We help individuals in [niche] manage their finances and reach their goals while overcoming challenges. [I invite you to set up a 30-minute virtual meeting with me. This will give me the chance to learn more about what you want from a financial advisor.] During our meeting, I will explain the services we offer at [Firm Name]. If you think my services might be a good fit for you, we can schedule a complimentary, in-depth discovery meeting to discuss your primary life goals. I will then suggest solutions to help you achieve those goals. [If this sounds good, please pick a time on my calendar [insert link].] In the meantime, I recommend reading [this article] about how fee-only services are different from traditional brokerage firms. My priority is to put your interests first and help you live your best life. I look forward to hearing from you. Warmly, [Your Name]

steps.name: Send Reminder Email
steps.description: Send a [reminder email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/422) , including an agenda for the introductory meeting and a [brief questionnaire](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/420) . Remind your prospect that the meeting's purpose is to learn about each other and determine a mutual fit for working towards their goals. Email Option: Dear [Prospect], Thank you for signing up for a 30-minute introductory meeting with me on [date and time] via [a Zoom invitation]. The intent of our meeting will be for me to learn how I might be able to assist you through my guidance and a comprehensive financial plan and for you to learn about my firm and the various engagement choices I offer. Our goal at the end of this complimentary meeting will be to determine if we want to schedule a deeper dive discovery meeting, in which I can learn about the nuances of your current situation and goals. I’ll also have time to reflect on our first discussions to share some possible high-level recommendations. At the end of the meeting, we should know enough to decide whether working together makes sense. Find attached a proposed agenda for our 30-minute meeting and a [brief questionnaire](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/420) to help me know you a bit better before we meet! I look forward to meeting with you on the [Date and Time] via [Zoom]. Warm regards, [Your Name]

steps.name: Hold Prospect Meeting
steps.description: Connect with your prospect in person, by phone, or through video. Use this opportunity to identify their needs and goals. The insights you gather will let you customize your services and offerings to align with their objectives. Present your firm's key attributes and pricing, then propose a 'deeper dive' Discovery meeting to explore further. Use this [meeting guide](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/372) to outline the agenda and key topics. Provide a [service calendar](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/1151) to show clients your dedication to their success and that support is provided in a timely manner throughout the year. Keep the meeting to about 30 minutes, using the 80/20 Rule: spend 80% of the time listening and 20% talking. If your prospect shows interest and values your offerings, you can extend the conversation as needed. Offer to schedule a time for their Discovery meeting if they are a good fit.

steps.name: Prospect Meeting Follow-Up
steps.description: Send an [email](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/423) to thank your prospect for their time, recap the main topics discussed, and share a relevant piece of content. Confirm the date and agenda for the upcoming Discovery meeting, and include some thoughtful questions for them to consider beforehand. If the prospect was a referral, send a thank-you note to your source. Email Option: Subject: Excited for Our Next Steps Together! Hi [Client's Name], I wanted to take a moment to express my heartfelt thanks for the wonderful meeting we had recently. It was great to explore our common ground and share ideas together. As we look ahead to our next meeting, I’m really looking forward to diving deeper into your financial goals and working together to create a personalized strategy just for you. It’s going to be an exciting journey! I’ve included an [ [agenda](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/371) ] for our meeting to provide clarity on the flow of our discussion and enhance our time together. Also, take a look at this [blog I wrote on a topic they expressed interest in.] Please feel free to reach out if you have any questions or need assistance with anything. I can’t wait to continue our conversation! Warm regards, [Your Name]

steps.name: Hold Discovery Meeting
steps.description: Identify your prospects' needs during this meeting. Brainstorm solutions for their main challenges and to address both short- and long-term goals. Apply the 80/20 Rule: spend 80% of the time listening and 20% talking during client conversations. Focus on understanding their needs, concerns, and goals. Use open-ended questions to encourage them to share more. This builds rapport and helps you tailor your solutions. Share relevant success stories to highlight your value. Use this agenda for [talking points](https://academy.xyplanningnetwork.com/share/asset/view/371) . Recap what you’ve discussed and show how you’ve supported others in similar situations. Ask if they need anything else to move forward. Aim for a verbal agreement and discuss the next steps before sending an electronic agreement for signing.

Send the follow-up information to convert your prospect into a client. Include your proposal from the meeting. Thank them for their trust and express your excitement about collaborating to achieve their goals! Encourage them to sign the agreement by a specific date so you can schedule a "Get Organized" meeting. Email Option: Dear [Client], I truly appreciate the opportunity to meet with you today! Your openness about your life goals was inspiring, and I am genuinely excited about the prospect of collaborating. I will be sending over the formal agreement for your electronic signature shortly. Once signed, we can arrange our first "Get Organized" meeting, during which I will guide you on the necessary documents to prepare. Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any questions before our meeting. Thank you for allowing me to be part of your journey toward achieving your goals! Best regards, [Your Name]

Dear [Client Name], I hope you’re having a great week! As we move into the year, we’re eager to share some intriguing topics and insights that will be the focus of our upcoming communications and activities. The first is understanding your cash flow and keeping a consistent budget. This is key towards reaching your financial goals. Regularly reviewing your income, expenses, and credit report can help you spot trends, catch potential issues early, and make confident decisions about saving and spending. If you would like assistance, wish to discuss any updates, or need some accountability to help you stay on track, please let us know. Thank you for your continued trust in us. Best regards, [email signature]

While I don't prepare taxes directly, I can coordinate with your tax preparer or assist you if you file yourself, ensuring they have all the necessary information regarding your investments and other relevant details. After your return is complete, we will review it together to identify planning opportunities, reduce future tax liability, and align your tax strategy with your long-term financial goals. Let me know if you need help gathering documents or if you’d like me to coordinate with your tax professional. Best, [Your Name]

Regularly reviewing your balance sheet and net worth help to ensure that your decisions align with your long-term goals. By examining your assets and liabilities, we can see if debt is helping you or if it is holding you back. This helps us find ways to lower interest costs, improve flexibility, and increase your net worth over time. If you have any questions or want to discuss this in detail, I’m happy to schedule some time. My goal is to make sure every part of your financial plan is aligned and moving you forward with confidence. Best regards, [Your Name]

These shifts are a critical time to reassess your disability, life, home, auto, and umbrella coverage to ensure your protection still aligns. If you’d like to discuss these topics or if there have been recent changes in your circumstances, I’d be happy to schedule some time with you. Thoughtful coordination can reduce risk and enhance your financial clarity! Best regards, [Your Name]

Email Option: Subject: Important Touchpoint for Your Estate Planning Dear [Client Name], As we continue our planning journey together, I wanted to reconnect about your estate plan and beneficiary designations. Let’s confirm that your beneficiary designations are up-to-date, evaluate essential documents like wills, trusts, powers of attorney, and advance healthcare directives, and explore gifting strategies that align with your aspirations and offer potential tax advantages. Whether you’ve experienced a recent life change or it has simply been a while since we last reviewed these items, now is an ideal time to ensure your coverage still aligns with your goals. Thoughtful planning in this area fosters clarity, continuity, and peace of mind for you and your loved ones. Please let us know if you’d like to have a conversation about any of these topics. Best regards, [Your Name]

localAnalyses.summary:
Redtail's basic (Launch) tier ($45) is not sufficient to cover most users' needs (notably workflows, calendar and email syncing are excluded), while Wealthbox's Basic tier ($59) includes most core features a user would need. At $65 per month, however, Redtail's Growth tier does include access to document storage, phone and text services, as well as compliant email archiving, which Wealthbox does not currently offer. 

Upgrading to the Pro plan on Wealthbox ($75) will provide access to enhanced features such as workflow milestones, contact roles and teams, email syncing, and custom dashboard creation. While upgrading to the Premier plan ($99) will give access to new internal automation features such as sending emails, making phone calls, filling forms and more. While Redtail's Growth plan ($65) technically offers internal automation, its functionality is limited.

One final notable feature Wealthbox now offers is built-in meeting transcription and AI note summarization. For an extra $49, Wealthbox will record and transcribe meeting notes, create summaries and itemize tasks without the use of 3rd party tools or Zaps needed.

Overall, we prefer Wealthbox for its ease of use, robust integration capabilities and excellent user support team, but which system works best for you will depend on your budget and which features you find most important.

localResources.name: One Year Anniversary Card Automation (1/2)
Document Needs List Generator - Upload Version
localResources.description:
This form serves as the foundation for document collection.

Needs List Generation: The team or client will answer the questions on the form to dynamically create a list of requested documents tailored to the client in question. This list will be sent to both clients and team member(s).

Uploading Documents: Documents will be uploaded directly to the form.

Processing Uploaded Documents (Not yet scoped): Direct upload will allow us to add an additional automation (or direct link) to add documents to your chosen File Storage System, including renaming and organizing them appropriately. Clients will be able to revisit the same link and continue uploading documents (or updating documents) after the first submission.

Reviewing Documents (Not yet scoped): This is not currently scoped, but we may incorporate a 'review' process where, as the team is reviewing the uploaded documents, they may indicate notes about the status of each item to send to the client. Once the team finishes entering notes and submits, clients can receive that feedback in real-time.

Document Reminders (Not yet scoped): This is not currently scoped, but we may create a 'reminder' process to alert clients of items still needed at a regular cadence. Similar to the AFD Follow Up Automation mentioned below.

Testable sample here

localResources.name: Birthday Card Automation (2/2)

localResources.description:
Build out an Excel sheet with three tabs to start - Birthday Card Approvals, Anniversary Card Approvals, Reference Sheet

Use formulas in both the Birthday and Anniversary card tabs to match the card type to the correct message content, font, card image and signature code for Handwrytten and format the salutation for one or both contacts.

Both the Birthday and Anniversary Card tabs will contain a Status column with three statuses (Approved, Needs Revision and Don't Send). If a status row is blank, Approved or Don't Send, the data in Cols B forward will be locked. If marked as Needs Revision the row will unlock and Cathy will be able to update the data before marking approved.

Once marked approved, the Part 2 (Birthday or Anniversary) automation will launch.

resources.description:
This form serves as the foundation for document collection.

Needs List Generation: The team or client will answer the questions on the form to dynamically create a list of requested documents tailored to the client in question. This list will be sent to both clients and team member(s).

Uploading Documents: Documents will be uploaded directly to the form.

Processing Uploaded Documents (Not yet scoped): Direct upload will allow us to add an additional automation (or direct link) to add documents to your chosen File Storage System, including renaming and organizing them appropriately. Clients will be able to revisit the same link and continue uploading documents (or updating documents) after the first submission.

Reviewing Documents (Not yet scoped): This is not currently scoped, but we may incorporate a 'review' process where, as the team is reviewing the uploaded documents, they may indicate notes about the status of each item to send to the client. Once the team finishes entering notes and submits, clients can receive that feedback in real-time.

Document Reminders (Not yet scoped): This is not currently scoped, but we may create a 'reminder' process to alert clients of items still needed at a regular cadence. Similar to the AFD Follow Up Automation mentioned below.

Testable sample here

resources.description:
Build out an Excel sheet with three tabs to start - Birthday Card Approvals, Anniversary Card Approvals, Reference Sheet

Use formulas in both the Birthday and Anniversary card tabs to match the card type to the correct message content, font, card image and signature code for Handwrytten and format the salutation for one or both contacts.

Both the Birthday and Anniversary Card tabs will contain a Status column with three statuses (Approved, Needs Revision and Don't Send). If a status row is blank, Approved or Don't Send, the data in Cols B forward will be locked. If marked as Needs Revision the row will unlock and Cathy will be able to update the data before marking approved.

Once marked approved, the Part 2 (Birthday or Anniversary) automation will launch.

steps.title: New File in Unfiled Receipts Folder

mappings.value:
Extract EACH ITEM from the receipt and provide the details as a JSON object suitable for logging in a Google Sheets spreadsheet using the Create Spreadsheet Row(s) action in Zapier.

Each object must contain the following fields: Date (yyyy-mm-dd), Vendor, Item Price, Quantity, Tax Rate (calculated from the total tax split over the percentage each item is of the total), Tax (calculated as Item Price * Quantity * Tax Rate), Total (calculated as Item Price * Quantity + Tax), Sub-Category (derived from predefined CATEGORIES), Item Name, and Account Used. Ensure that the data is formatted correctly for each column header.

The date is most likely in the file name if not sure. If not included in the file name, do your best to extract as a final resort, favoring the current year unless it is January then the preceding year.

If tax is returned as a separate line item only use it to check the values for each individual item. Don't return it as its own object but DO include the tax rate and item tax for each other item.

Finally, generate a file name as YYYY-MM-DD_Vendor Name.

localAnalyses.summary:
Redtail's basic (Launch) tier ($45) is not sufficient to cover most users' needs (notably workflows, calendar and email syncing are excluded), while Wealthbox's Basic tier ($59) includes most core features a user would need. At $65 per month, however, Redtail's Growth tier does include access to document storage, phone and text services, as well as compliant email archiving, which Wealthbox does not currently offer. 

Upgrading to the Pro plan on Wealthbox ($75) will provide access to enhanced features such as workflow milestones, contact roles and teams, email syncing, and custom dashboard creation. While upgrading to the Premier plan ($99) will give access to new internal automation features such as sending emails, making phone calls, filling forms and more. While Redtail's Growth plan ($65) technically offers internal automation, its functionality is limited.

One final notable feature Wealthbox now offers is built-in meeting transcription and AI note summarization. For an extra $49, Wealthbox will record and transcribe meeting notes, create summaries and itemize tasks without the use of 3rd party tools or Zaps needed.

Overall, we prefer Wealthbox for its ease of use, robust integration capabilities and excellent user support team, but which system works best for you will depend on your budget and which features you find most important.

localResources.description:
Monthly Advisor Report

Automation that launches when a new meeting is added to Outlook (via OnceHub sync or manually using template) and synced to the Wealthbox calendar.

The automation will extract the event details including invitee email, name and phone, meeting type and location. Then, the automation will add a row to the Meeting KPI Tracking spreadsheet for report creation.

Agenda Email Creation

This part of the automation will take the extracted event data and search for a matching event category between Outlook and Wealthbox. If found, the Wealthbox event will be updated to the correct category. If not, the team will be notified that a match could not be found.

Next, the automation will search for a household or contact record in Wealthbox first by email, then fall back to name. If still not found, the automation can either create a new contact (or household) or notify the team.

If a contact (or household) was found in the prior step (or created) it will be synced to the event record. If found (existing) the following datapoints will be extracted:

  • Client preferred name(s)
  • Primary email address for client and (if applicable) spouse
  • Primary phone number for client and (if applicable) spouse
  • Meeting date and time
  • Meeting location
  • Trusted contact name (if tagged) or note to provide a trusted contact (if not tagged)

These datapoints will be used to draft a Meeting Agenda Email in the assigned advisor's Outlook Drafts box. Then the automation will create a task to review, revise and send this draft, assigned to the same advisor.

Meeting Prep Information Import

Additionally, the automation will pull these datapoints from the contact record if found:

  • Kids/Pet Names
  • Security Questions
  • MyRepChat
  • PII Form 456
  • Trusted Contact F451
  • POA on FIle

Based on the type of meeting, the automation will pull the relevant form(s) from Cognito Form and link to the client's most recent submission:

  • Fit Meeting Questionnaire (Fit Meeting)
  • Financial Planning Intake Form
  • BMG Advisors Document Uploads

Next, it will search for the client's folder in Box and return the link. Optionally it will search within the Box folder for the most recent file including Tax Return in the name and return the link for that file.

CRM meeting notes, advisor notes, important client reminders and other relevant info will be extracted from the most recent *prior* meeting scheduled's description.

Finally, the automation will use these details to create a prefilled Excel Meeting Prep document in the client's Box folder before creating a Wealthbox task assigned to the advisor to update the Meeting Prep document.

localResources.name: Onboarding Email (Welcome Party)
localResources.emailBody:
Hi {firstName} and happy Friday!

Thanks for your time earlier this week and being so open to sharing your thoughts and concerns. I'm excited to work with you and your family and hep you through this transition as well as long-term! More information form me as we get started together. I've attached your welcome party that outlines what to expect during the onboarding process. Most of it is informational but shoot me any quesitons!

As far as next steps together, you'll receive two emails as we get started:

1 - Data Gathering Questionnaire requesting additional information to open new Schwab accounts for you, including your date of birth, Social Security number, et.

2 - Wealth Advisory Agreement outlining fees, terms of working together and other general legal language. This will come from Schwab's DocuSign platform.

You have multiple ways to add any additional information you haven't already provided. You can upload directly in the questionnaire when prompted or via the secure link below in my signature.

Thanks and looking forward to it!
Ally

Lindsey

localResources.emailBody:
Thank you for our discussion today. It was a pleasure meeting you and I look forward to engaging with you in the Discover process.

A few follow-up items:

1) Next meeting: As discussed, our next meeting is scheduled for [date]. You should have received a calendar invite from Calendly with the meeting information. Please let me know if you did not receive that invite.

2) Today's presentation: I have attached a copy of today's presentation for your reference.

3) Disclosures: Please see below a link to the disclosures for XYPN Sapphire:

https://xypnsapphire.com/disclosures

4) Data request list: I have attached a list of items that I will be requesting in our next meeting. Please be prepared to download these items during our next meeting.

5) Risk tolerance assessment: I would like each of you to take a risk tolerance assessment at some point in the next couple of weeks. Each of you should take your own individual assessment without assistance from your spouse. Answer the questions to the best of your ability. This assessment should take about 15-20 minutes. The links to your individual assessments are below:

6) Client portal: I use a financial planning software application called eMoney Advisor as part of my practice. This is a collaborative tool that includes a client portal with a number of features. I will send you an invite to this software tool. Feel free to log in and set up your account, but there is no need to go through the onboarding process - we can do that together in a couple of weeks, and I will also proved at that time some training on this platform.

Thank you again for choosing to engage with me, and I look forward to meeting you again in a couple of weeks.

Best,
Lindsey

steps.description: Touch base with prospect via call if you have their cell number and if not by email. Have a basic script of questions to pose your prospect or a message ready to leave on a voice mail to work to engage your lead, remembering that your conversations should focus primarily on 'why' they are contacting you and how you'd like to explore if there is a fit for working together in an Introductory Prospect Fit meeting. Keep in mind that your goal is to schedule that first meeting, converting your lead to an interested prospect.
steps.name: Lead to Prospect 7
Lead to Prospect 8
steps.description: Consider this step a last attempt and reach out again to your lead with relevant content. Share that you consider they're not presently interested in working with you but that you are available when they are. Share some additional relevant material and wish them well. They are then moved to the 'Drip Campaign' of less frequent communications, but to keep additional information and educational resources coming to them sporadically, to hopefully engage them further when they are ready.

Also referred to as an Introductory Prospect Fit meeting, this step is to have an 'in person', on the phone or via video conferencing to learn and ask questions to understanding the needs, fears, challenges and goals of your now prospect. The more you learn here the more you'll know what to share about your services and what content to share verbally to know how best to help them and to eventually gain their business. See attached a sample agenda for the meeting and key talking points. Find as well an example of a handout of your services which you might share. This meeting should typically take no longer than 30 minutes though may take longer if your prospect has immediate interest and sees and feels your value based on what you share with regard to other people you've helped in similar situations. Tip: This meeting should take no more than 30 minutes unless you feel a close to client status is imminent, in which case you and your prospect agree to taking longer than initially planned when you set up the meeting.
steps.name: Hold Prospect Meeting
Prospect Follow-Up Email
steps.description: Thank your prospect for a great meeting and share your excitement over the synergies revealed. If you didn't in a pre-Introductory Prospect Fit meeting email send a short questionnaire to learn some information about your prospect, you might do so here. (Assure the questions are not lengthy as this could turn off your client before building greater rapport together). If you did not put a next time to meet on the calendar when you last were together, send along a Calendly invite to do so or include a reminder of the time you discussed. You might share as well in your meeting and send afterward, your service calendar or a relevant piece of content that relates to topics discussed in your Introductory Prospect Fit meeting. You might send as well an agenda for your upcoming Discovery meeting and question categories to discuss in your 'deeper dive' next meeting.

Hold your Discovery meeting. Go more deeply into learning about your prospect and their needs. Begin to map out a plan of action for working to shore up their key challenges and to work toward meeting their most pressing short and long term goals. Use stories to share your value of how you've helped others. A Discovery meeting agenda and talking points are attached. Toward the end of your meeting plan to review all that was discussed in your two meetings and build a case on how you're served others in perhaps a similar situation in the past or share your experience in your niche group that they fall into. Let them know you'd be honored to work with them and find out if there is anything else they need from you to make a decision now to move forward together. Close the sales with a verbal agreement and plan next steps together for reviewing a proposal of services before sending an electronic agreement for them to sign.
steps.name: Hold Discovery Meeting

steps.description: Send an email with necessary follow-up information to convert your prospect to a client. Thank them for their trust in you and express excitement in working with them to reach their goals and/or to get passed a pressing and challenging situation. Assure to create a sense of urgency and excitement for helping your new client to reach their goals. Be sure as well to set a deadline for having your agreement for working together signed so you can schedule out a 'Get Organized' meeting, letting your prospect know that sharing confidential financial information can't officially begin until they have a secured agreement. See a sample email communication to send after your Discovery meeting attached below.

Share that you consider they're not presently interested in working with you but that you are available when they are. Share some additional relevant material and wish them well. They are then moved to the 'Drip Campaign' of less frequent communications, but to keep additional information and educational resources coming to them sporadically, to hopefully engage them further when they are ready.

steps.name: Hold Prospect Meeting
steps.description: Also referred to as an Introductory Prospect Fit meeting, this step is to have an 'in person', on the phone or via video conferencing to learn and ask questions to understanding the needs, fears, challenges and goals of your now prospect. The more you learn here the more you'll know what to share about your services and what content to share verbally to know how best to help them and to eventually gain their business. See attached a sample agenda for the meeting and key talking points. Find as well an example of a handout of your services which you might share. This meeting should typically take no longer than 30 minutes though may take longer if your prospect has immediate interest and sees and feels your value based on what you share with regard to other people you've helped in similar situations. Tip: This meeting should take no more than 30 minutes unless you feel a close to client status is imminent, in which case you and your prospect agree to taking longer than initially planned when you set up the meeting.

steps.name: Prospect Follow-Up Email
steps.description: Thank your prospect for a great meeting and share your excitement over the synergies revealed. If you didn't in a pre-Introductory Prospect Fit meeting email send a short questionnaire to learn some information about your prospect, you might do so here. (Assure the questions are not lengthy as this could turn off your client before building greater rapport together). If you did not put a next time to meet on the calendar when you last were together, send along a Calendly invite to do so or include a reminder of the time you discussed. You might share as well in your meeting and send afterward, your service calendar or a relevant piece of content that relates to topics discussed in your Introductory Prospect Fit meeting. You might send as well an agenda for your upcoming Discovery meeting and question categories to discuss in your 'deeper dive' next meeting.

steps.name: Hold Discovery Meeting
steps.description: Hold your Discovery meeting. Go more deeply into learning about your prospect and their needs. Begin to map out a plan of action for working to shore up their key challenges and to work toward meeting their most pressing short and long term goals. Use stories to share your value of how you've helped others. A Discovery meeting agenda and talking points are attached. Toward the end of your meeting plan to review all that was discussed in your two meetings and build a case on how you're served others in perhaps a similar situation in the past or share your experience in your niche group that they fall into. Let them know you'd be honored to work with them and find out if there is anything else they need from you to make a decision now to move forward together. Close the sales with a verbal agreement and plan next steps together for reviewing a proposal of services before sending an electronic agreement for them to sign.

steps.name: Discovery Meeting Follow-Up
steps.description: Send an email with necessary follow-up information to convert your prospect to a client. Thank them for their trust in you and express excitement in working with them to reach their goals and/or to get passed a pressing and challenging situation. Assure to create a sense of urgency and excitement for helping your new client to reach their goals. Be sure as well to set a deadline for having your agreement for working together signed so you can schedule out a 'Get Organized' meeting, letting your prospect know that sharing confidential financial information can't officially begin until they have a secured agreement. See a sample email communication to send after your Discovery meeting attached below.

Once you have a signed agreement from your now client, send a list of documents they'll need to send to you for your Get Organized meeting. Find attached a follow up email once your agreement is signed. Congratulations on securing a new client! It's now time to move to your Get Organized meeting workflow!

Please bring with you whatever financial information you can easily put your hands on. If you just want to bring in a box full of scattered papers (or even unopened envelopes!), that's absolutely fine. If your accounts are mostly set up online, we’ll help you track those down too."

steps.name: Conduct Intro Call
steps.description: Reminders: All forms are linked in the custom fields section on the household record Ask questions, then listen! Let the prospect share their story. If you aren't clear about something or need more info, ask for clarification. Current Step: Access the Meeting Notes Form in the custom fields section of the household record 15 mins before the call begins. At the start of the call, set the tone and agenda. This ensures the meeting will stay on track and instills confidence. During the call, use the form to dynamically walk through the process. Answer each question as it appears to show the next relevant question. At the end of the call, give the prospect an opportunity to ask questions or add comments, then touch base on how they are feeling about next steps and what their desired timeframe to move forward (or not) is. Enter the outcome and, if applicable, the agreed-upon follow up date. Immediately after the call, clean up the action items and email summary. Submit the form to automatically add the notes to the Wealthbox household, itemize the team's tasks in Wealthbox and send the summary email to the prospect(s). Next Steps Summary: Update the workflow with the outcome of the meeting and follow the next steps depending on the outcome.

steps.description: Check prior year and YTD performance in Black Diamond to confirm it looks as expected. If performance does not look as expected, review positions and cash inflows/outflows to determine the cause. If still unclear, review with Tammy. If the client has a margin balance, confirm that it is marked unsupervised. In Client Setup -> Accounts, search for the account with a margin balance, then click the account number Navigate to Holdings, then look for the cash holding (total units will be negative) Check the box to the left of the Asset ID, then click Edit 1 Holding Change from Supervised to Unsupervised, click continue, then click Save in the top right If the client has cash set aside in Schwab money market, confirm with Tammy the purpose of funds and if it should be included in the allocation. Review the current allocation vs. Target allocation to confirm that it is in-line. If not, review accounts/notes to determine why. If still unclear, review with Tammy. Initiate any cash invest or rebalancing trades that should be placed prior to the meeting.
steps.name: Review Accounts

steps.description: Review accounts in [Right Capital](https://app.rightcapital.com/account/login) linked through [Black Diamond](https://bd3.bdreporting.com/#/) Confirm that all necessary accounts are feeding into the plan. If there are accounts missing, review the portfolio in Black Diamond and add accounts as necessary. If there are accounts that are not relevant to the financial plan, create a new portfolio in Black Diamond - RC - Last Name, First Name - to include only the necessary accounts Update Account Name using proper [naming conventions](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1FrgbQE3XDgIQ24syWImaxLyMsPrZHlYtOXmi1guCEh8/edit?gid=604843894#gid=604843894) if needed. Review Connections - if the client has connected any of their bank or outside investment accounts, refresh the connections to make sure they are still live. Review and update property details - search the address on Zillow. Update the following: Purchase year if not already in the plan Current value Annual property tax HOA fees Review and update margin loan balance and rate. Refer to [naming conventions](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1FrgbQE3XDgIQ24syWImaxLyMsPrZHlYtOXmi1guCEh8/edit?gid=1271682847#gid=1271682847) for appropriate Account Name Review Insurance to determine if there are any whole life policies that need to be updated Send Right Capital Client Access invite if not already sent. Send Annual Review Meeting Prep email to client(s). Edit the template to only include data relevant to the client
steps.name: Review Right Capital and Email Client for Updated Information
Review Prior Year Recommendations and Open Tasks to Set Agenda
steps.description: Save a copy of the [Annual Review Agenda](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ni4KWYkK0w3yJ5lKqDjmrSjduty1oWGO/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=109384278514143926952&rtpof=true&sd=true) to the client's financial planning folder. Add any questions/concerns/updates related to the client's managed investment accounts, allocation, or cash balances Add any questions or updates needed related to the financial plan assumptions Add loss carryforward and prior year realized gain/loss Locate loss carryfoward on the client's tax return - if the number on Schedule D, line 16 is negative, subtract $3,000. That is the loss carryforward Prior year gain/loss is found in Schwab - add the gain/loss for all of the client's taxable accounts Open the account in Schwab, then navigate to Cost Basis View Realized Gain/(Loss), change the period to Prior Year, click apply filter. steps.description: Call with the client to contra firm to find out their process for moving 401k/457/403b/Annuity/Pension funds etc. Find out transfer method and eligibility Ask whether the funds can be moved via a direct rollover (trustee-to-trustee transfer). This is the safest option. “Do you support a direct rollover to a Schwab IRA?” “Will the check be made payable to Schwab FBO (client name), or sent electronically?” “Are there any restrictions on rolling over my specific plan?” Required paperwork and steps “What forms do I need to complete to initiate the rollover?” “Can this be done online, or do I need physical forms/signatures?” “Does Schwab need to submit anything to you, or do I initiate everything from your side?” “Do you require a letter of acceptance from Schwab?” Processing time and tracking “What is your typical processing timeline from request to completion?” “How will I know when the funds have been sent?” “Is there a tracking number if a check is mailed?” Fees and withholding “Are there any fees for processing the rollover?” “Will any taxes be withheld automatically, or is it processed as a full rollover with no withholding?” (You want confirmation there is no 20% withholding if done correctly as a direct rollover.) Liquidation of investments “Do I need to liquidate my investments before the transfer, or will you do that?” “How long does liquidation take before funds are available to transfer?” Check handling details (if applicable) “How exactly will the check be titled?” (Important: should be payable to Schwab, not the client personally) “Will the check be mailed to me or directly to Schwab?” “If mailed to client, are there any special instructions for forwarding it?” Account and contribution details “Will this be coded as a rollover (not a distribution) on your end?” “Will the client receive a 1099-R, and how will it be coded?” (You want it coded as a rollover, not taxable distribution.) “Are there any after-tax or Roth funds in my account that need special handling?” Special situations “Are there any blackout periods, pending transactions, or restrictions that could delay the transfer?” “Do I need spousal consent or employer approval?” (Sometimes required for certain plans.) Contact and follow-up “Who should I contact if there are delays or issues?” “Is there a direct department or case number I should reference?”
